noi_dung:
Introduction

An Si Complete Book is a book promoting charity that has been praised many times by Master An Quang. He personally mobilized and organized the printing and circulation, with the number reaching tens of thousands of volumes. Therefore, the first time I came into contact with this book in Chinese, I couldn't help but have some concerns and questions.

Why do I have concerns and questions? Because when looking through the general catalog of this book, what stands out is the section Sound quality of writing advertisement, which is based on the essay Sound quality by Wenchang Dejun to explain extensively. The remaining parts are Western Guidance, Van Thien Tien Tu and Desire Sea Returns to the Wild which may not be discussed for now, but as for the Sound substance text, it seems not to be part of the Buddha's Dharma.

Wenchang Dijun is a fictional character. Although part of the legend about him can be temporarily considered true, there are countless things woven around his image, most of which are ignorant, unintelligent, if not superstitious beliefs. So, are the words passed down from such a figure worthy of Buddhists' attention and study?

Is such a book worth widely circulating?...

But Master An Quang was originally a dragon statue in Buddhism. His life and career are more than enough for us to put our trust in his advice. The great master spoke about the book The Complete Book of An Si and its author, Mr. Chu An Si, as follows:

“...truly a book that promotes the best in the world, if compared to other ordinary books on promoting good deeds, can it be compared? My heart still firmly believes that you must be a Bodhisattva according to the original I vow to appear as a lay person to preach Dharma to save sentient beings.”

(Excerpt from Master An Quang's Preface)

It was my belief in Master An Quang that encouraged me to continue reading the book An Si Complete Book, instead of putting it aside after realizing the presence of a character called Wenchang Dejun.

And indeed I was not mistaken in my faith. After reading the content of the book, I understood the reason why the Great Master was full of praise, and also saw the compassion and wonderful wisdom of Mr. Chu An Si when composing this book of encouragement.

From then on, I devoted myself to translating this book into Vietnamese, at the same time compiling annotations and correcting some errors in the main text to make the book more complete. The book is thicker than thousands of pages of large-format Chinese text, using many classics and techniques

Confucian and Taoist languages ​​and quoted a large number of Classics. With a huge amount of reference material and under the interrogation conditions of the 17th century, the author could not avoid quoting or quoting scriptures in many places that were not entirely accurate. During the translation process, we tried our best to discover and clearly note these points to help readers access a more complete text. Therefore, the entire work of reviewing, translating and annotating had to last for nearly two years.

Regarding the book's content, the author relied on the very brief Acoustics essay (only about 800 words) to compile a book with more than 400 pages of large-sized Chinese characters. The presentation is quite consistent throughout the book. For every sentence that is analyzed, there is always an extensive lecture that he calls “discovery minh”, followed by a section of comments and discussions, which he calls “judgment”. Next, most of them have an additional section citing stories, including stories drawn from the classics or Buddhist stories, for the purpose of illustrating the meaning of the above sections.

It is Mr. An Si's extensive lectures and comments that have explored and expanded the meaning of the text completely in the spirit of Buddhism, helping readers thereby receive quintessential teachings and good knowledge in the spirit of compassion, altruism and wisdom. It is not difficult for us to realize that, although

is based on the essay Sound Essence, most of Mr. An Si's writings have completely dominated the content of this book.

A question can be raised at this point: Why do you have to rely on the essay Sound Essence? Why don't you write all of that content yourself, which is not difficult considering the effort you put into this book?

Please tell me, that is where the wonderful means of Buddha Dharma are, where the scriptures have taught: “All all dharmas are Buddha dharma.” If we recall that among those who do not really have a deep understanding of Buddhism, nine out of ten always have faith in the gods of heaven and earth. The belief in Wenchang Dijun was that kind of belief. Perhaps Mr. An Si himself would never really choose to follow or care about these kinds of beliefs. However, with compassion, he realized that there are many people who are clinging to those beliefs as their refuge in life, and requiring or advising them to deny or reject those beliefs without having more insight and awareness to replace them would be unthinkable, and could even have unintended, opposite effects. That's why he chose an extremely unique method, based on this existing belief, to lead readers towards the Dharma. Every sentence and every word written by him in this book is imbued with the spirit of Buddhism,

step by step leads the reader onto the path of profound faith and a deep understanding of the meanings of good and evil, cause and effect... Therefore, Master An Quang's comments are certainly not arbitrary.

Furthermore, the deeper I go into the content of the book, the more I feel more confident in the above comments, as well as the more I realize the boundless benefits of this book to promote goodness, especially in today's era of confusion between good and evil.

In terms of method, it can be said that Mr. has compiled this book in a very meticulous and scientific way. Just looking at the reference list of scriptures of all three religions (Buddhism, Taoism, Confucianism) including 126 sets of scriptures of all kinds and recalling that he lived around the end of the 17th century, we will greatly admire his interrogation and filtering from this huge number of scriptures. Furthermore, most of the quotes in the book are taken from the Buddhist scriptures, showing his erudition about the Inner Canon and further increasing the faith-establishing value of this book.

However, the compilation process cannot avoid some small limitations and defects, such as some stories taken from the Classics are rewritten instead of quoted verbatim, but sometimes there are a few details that are not completely accurate. In these cases, when Vietnamese translates, we also compare the scriptures according to the author's notes to edit them for more accuracy.

In addition, sometimes we encounter inaccurate annotations, when the author does not directly take from the scripture but quotes from another document, and the document itself has confusion, leading to errors. In these cases, we will try to find the correct part of the original text as a basis, and add appropriate comments to clarify this confusion, avoiding future people from continuing to misunderstand.

For Sutra annotations, we will try to add in the commentary the necessary details related to the cited sutra, such as sutra number in the Mahaskaya Pitaka, page number, line number where the quoted Sutra passage appears, etc. With this information, when the reader needs to compare and consult any issue in the book, it will be much easier.

Finally, with sincere gratitude to the author for leaving behind a precious book, we would like to widely introduce the Vietnamese translation and commentary of this book to all those who are predestined, hoping that we can continue and further expand his wish to save sentient beings. Please pray for us to have enough favorable conditions to continue to complete the rest of the book series in the near future, contributing to bringing benefit and happiness to everyone.

Sincerely,

Nguyen Minh Iprove

FOREWORD ENGRAVING THE REPRINT OF THE BOOK
AN SI TOAN THU

(This preface was written by Master An Quang

in the year Mau Ngo - 1918)

For all sentient beings, the two karmas of lust and killing are the basis of the cycle of birth and death. The hardest thing to get rid of is lust, and the easiest thing to commit is killing. Of these two things, when it comes to lust, anyone with some intelligence can self-examine and refrain from committing it. However, if you want your mind to be pure and completely cut off to the subtle source of lust, only an Arhat has eliminated all defilements and attained true nature. Those who have not been like that must all carry the habit of craving, even if it is somewhat severe, more or less different. Therefore, day by day, desire becomes more and more solidified in the mind, life after life, unable to reach liberation.

When it comes to killing, people all consider it a matter of course, using the strong to bully the weak, using the flesh and blood of living beings to fill their stomachs, only knowing the temporary appetite but no one believes in having to pay back in eternity. The Shurangama Sutra teaches that: “People eat

goat meat, goats die and are reborn as humans, people who die are reborn as goats, until all living beings are born and died revolving like that, eating and devouring each other, creating negative karma forever!”1

NOTE 1

Actually, this passage is indirectly excerpted from the Surangama Sutra Sutra (首楞嚴義疏注經), which is classified in the Dai Chanh Tan Tu Canon, volume 39, sutra number 1799, compiled by Mr. Tu Tuyen in the Song Dynasty. This book has 20 volumes. This excerpt belongs to volume 7, starting from line 21, page 877, sheet b.

The ancients taught that:

If you want peace in the world,
You must stop eating the flesh of all living beings.

It also teaches that:

If you want to know why the world,
Continuous fire, countless disasters,
Listen to the echo of the long night,
The pitiful cries of all living beings.
Behold, in the slaughterhouse,
All species perished because of me!

Therefore, no matter how the cause is created, the result must be like that. If you don't think, you can still commit a crime. If you have thought, you must be terrified and not dare to kill again!

Mr. An Si2 respectfully obeyed the Buddha's teachings, developed a heart of compassion for all people, and composed the book

NOTE 2

That is, layman Chu An Si (周安士), born in 1656, died in 1739, was a famous scholar in the early Qing Dynasty of China, real name was Chu Mong Nhan (周梦顏), other name was Tu Nhan (思仁). He deeply believed in the Western Pure Land dharma for life, so he took the nickname Hoai Tay Layman (怀西居士).

Duc Hai Hoi Crazy (欲海回狂) to advise against lust, book Van Thien Tien Tu (萬善先資) to advise against killing. It cites real events, clearly shows cause and effect, and hopes that all people in this world will treat each other like brothers born from heaven and earth; People and all species have the same true mind, forever eliminating the evil mind that causes moral harm, goes against morality, and relies on the strong to oppress the weak. Also, in order to join everyone in not committing evil and diligently doing good deeds, we should take the essay Yin quality (陰騭文) by Wenchang Dijun and add detailed notes, called Yin quality literature (陰騭文廣義), so that people can follow this and keep it in all their daily actions. Kindness in behavior, for example, on a large scale, can rule the country and protect the people, but on a small scale, every word and every thought must be carefully considered and compatible with morality.

For the teachings of such ancient sages, one must be very respectful and careful, read through and contemplate with the right mind, with a sincere will, not those who just discuss it can understand it.

All three of the above-mentioned books, interesting literature, are well versed in things from the past, beneficial to life and people, that is thanks to him using his excellent talent, combined with profound insight, understanding the mind dharma of the Buddhas and Saints and then using pen and ink to convey the truth to people, promoting what he has understood.

However, even if one can abstain from lust, abandon the karma of killing, not commit evil, and diligently do good deeds, if one has not yet achieved ultimate liberation from the cycle of birth and death, how can one avoid being reborn forever and ever? You can only try to keep from letting go, and you will always be born in good realms, cultivate wisdom, and not fall into bad realms. Not many people can achieve that, let alone understanding the truth of life and death and escaping reincarnation. Isn't that an easy thing to talk about? It is necessary to rely on the power of cultivating concentration and wisdom, eliminating defilements, and attaining true nature in order to achieve ultimate freedom and liberation. All those who have not been like that, only thanks to merit, can be born as kings of the heavens, as high as the heaven of Phi Phi Phien, enjoy blessings and live for up to 80,000 great eons, 1 but even so, they are still bound in the cycle of karma, depending on good and evil karma, they must forever be reborn in samsara.

NOTE 1

Great eon: a period of time that is too long to count. In Buddhist scriptures, there are five examples of the duration of a great kalpa, called the five examples of the great kalpa (大劫五喻), including herb example (e.g., number of plants and trees), sa tei example (e.g., number of fine grains of sand), worldly example (e.g., number of mustard seeds), tanh mundan example (e.g., number of dust particles) and whittling stone (like time wiping away a large rock). All five of these examples are intended to show that the duration of a great kalpa is very long, beyond our ability to imagine and count.

Therefore, according to the method taught by the Tathagata, that by relying on the Buddha's compassion, even if karma has not ended, one can still be reborn, Mr. An Si immediately took the essential meanings of the sutras and treatises on the Pure Land and combined them to compose a book, named

Tai Quy Truong Chi (西歸直指). Anyone who can read that book once will have deep and strong faith and eliminate all doubts. If you start a mind of faith and make a vow to be reborn in the Western world, regardless of whether your base is good or slow, the karma you have created is heavy or light, your practice is deep or shallow, as long as you have enough faith, make a sincere and sincere vow, recite the Buddha's name, then surely at the time of death you will rely on the Buddha's compassionate guidance to be reborn.

When he is reborn, of course he has left the mortal world to become a saint, fully comprehending the meaning of death and birth, liberating himself from reincarnation. In just one thought, he will realize his own mind, and the attainment of Enlightenment will surely come soon. Such beneficial meanings can only be known by those who have truly attained it. They cannot be described in literary language.

The essence of this method is to use the deep faith and vow of the practitioner to harmonize with the compassionate mind of the Buddha, thanks to which such immense benefits can be obtained. If compared with using one's own strength to eliminate defilements, attain true nature, fully understand the truth of birth and death, and overcome reincarnation, the level of difficulty is truly as different as heaven and earth!

Currently1 in the world there are countries in constant war, people in the country [China] are divided into north and south from disagreement, attacking each other. In addition, in recent years, there have been natural disasters like storms, floods, droughts, earthquakes, robberies, epidemics... I often hear news about the statistics of internal and external casualties

NOTE 1

That was in 1918, when this title article was written.

under tens of thousands of people, causing immense pain in my heart, I don't know what to do, I hate myself for being incompetent and unintelligent, I abuse being in the ranks of the monks but have not yet attained enlightenment, I only have a heart of love for life and people, I really have no strength to save.

There is a compatriot in Can Pho, Mr. Luu Tai Tieu, who is a noble scholar, whose family has passed down morality for many generations, and who believes deeply in Buddhism. This summer, he went to the mountain to meet and ask for guidance. When discussing together the current situation in the country and abroad, he suddenly worriedly asked: “Teacher, is there any magical method that can help?”

I replied: “That is the karmic effect of suffering, and that suffering must have a cause. If you want to save suffering, you must eliminate the cause of suffering. Once the cause is eliminated, the effect will not arise from anywhere . Therefore, Buddhist scriptures teach: 'Bodhisattvas fear the cause, living beings fear the effect.''

Therefore, he immediately showed the book An Si Complete Book to him, hoping to have it engraved and circulated widely, allowing everyone who reads it to escape samsara and go straight to the shore of enlightenment. He could not contain his joy, immediately called his nephew Trieu Bo Van and took out 700 coins, hoping that I would help with the engraving. I remember that in the year Mau Than (1908) I advised Ly Thien Que to engrave and print this book in Shu.1 he immediately asked me to write the foreword, but then there was not enough favorable conditions so in the end it failed.

NOTE 1

That is Sichuan region (四川).

Now thanks to Mr. Liu's determination to help, it is a great opportunity, I immediately added the following texts to engrave and print:

- The book Lieu Pham's Four Instructions (了凡四訓) by Vien Lieu

Pham, are beautiful words that advise giving up evil and doing good.

- A memoir by Du Tinh Y,1 extremely thoughtful words

NOTE 1

That is, the book Du Tinh Y Cong Enlightens the Divine Records (俞净意公遇灶神記).

City, penetrating the deep and beautiful places in heaven and earth, promoting the meaning of everything, advising people to persevere in their efforts, is the most pure, beautiful and dignified place, clearly revealed.

These two books are added after the lower book of the Sound quality of popular literature section.

- The essay The Precept to Kill and Release Life (戒殺放生文) by Great Master

Lien Tri, who can be considered a compassionate master who eliminates cruel demons, is now added after the book Van Thien Tien tu.

- The chants in the collection Impure Contemplation (不淨觀) by

Dharma Master Tinh Am, who can be considered a brave general of pure conduct to eliminate the demons of desire, are now added after the book The sea of ​​desire returns to madness.

- The essay Khuyên to develop the mind of Bodhisattva (勸發菩提心文)

also by Mr. Tinh Am, can be considered a magnetic boat to save sentient beings in the sea of ​​suffering in samsara, now added after the book Western Guidance.

Mr. An Si's three volumes of books were added to such sections, just like the brocade

beautiful and embroidered with flowers, like a light placed next to a mirror, the flower-colored light becomes even more brilliant, making everyone's hearts happy. Indeed, for those who skillfully read this book, the cruel and deceitful thoughts will immediately disappear, and the wishes to benefit others will naturally arise, from contemplation, gradually moving towards goodness, making deeper and deeper progress. Even without paying attention, the mundane mind will naturally gradually transform into the wisdom of a saint, almost reaching the point of understanding the truth of life and death, forever escaping samsara, and being able to face and worship Amitābha Buddha. I received a prediction from Buddha.

After reading this book with respect, there is a joyful chant:

Long submerged in the sea of ​​karma,
Suddenly met a magnetic boat. Harmony and touch the color path,
Amitābha Buddha is nearby.

In addition, please read more in the preface article written in the year Mau Than (1908), now not copied cumbersomely.

The 7th year of the Republic (1918),

Mau Ngo, June 19.

Co Tan Thich An Quang respectfully inscribed.1

NOTE 1

Master An Quang's birth date January 11, 1862, died December 2, 1940, was revered as the 13th Patriarch of the Chinese Pure Land Sect, and made many important contributions to the revitalization of Buddhism in China in general and the Pure Land sect in particular. The great master in many other works also often signed his name as Co Tan Thuong Tam Quy Tang Thich An Quang (古莘常惭愧僧释印光). He knew the day of his passing away, so he invited the four disciples to gather together and advised them to deeply believe in the Buddha's recitation method. Then he sat down in the lotus position, recited Buddha's name with the crowd for a moment, and then peacefully passed away. Contemporaries believed that he was the reincarnation of Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva.

FOREWORD WRITTEN IN THE YEAR OF THE MOTHER
(1908)

(Written at the request
of the layperson of Shu, Ly Thien Que)

Low great! My mind is inherently full of righteousness! What a miracle! Our mind inherently has wonderful dharma!

It has always been quietly shining without discrimination; The true path is all peaceful. Get rid of all thoughts, get rid of all emotions; neither born nor destroyed. Say there isthat but not there; but doesn't have but has. Say no that's not no; Although not no but no. All living Buddhas have arisen from there, neither saints nor ordinary people can be named. Like a shining mirror from ancient times, there is not a single object, but countless scenes of Han and Ho appear. Like vast space far away from all forms, there is no need to worry when the sun shines or the clouds cover it. That is the ultimate reality, without any dust; Even in this unenlightened mind, all dharmas are included, such as the place of attaining supreme enlightenment of the Buddhas, as well as the place of confusion and not recognizing the eternal true mind of sentient beings.

The saints in the Three Teachings all followed this same mentality and compassionately taught and guided many ignorant sentient beings. Because of this meaning, Confucius1 proposed the theory of "success", choosing sincerity and wisdom as the basis of wisdom, from which he proposed rules to improve and regulate peace;2 Lao Tzu3 published the book Tao Te Ching, teaching the law of living a long and peaceful life. The Enlightened One, the World-Honored One, clearly stated the nature of the Dharma realm, showed the true mind, taught the true path of letting go of the mortal world and returning to Enlightenment, establishing the principle of no birth no death. Although the large and small shallows and depths are not the same, there are differences between the worldly world and the transcendent world, but all of them are beyond the common point that right in this mind of us is full of all dharmas. Promoting and widely teaching this Dharma to all sentient beings, starting from the place of self-nature, is aimed at revealing self-nature, cutting off all illusory thoughts, returning to the inherent true self-nature, forever escaping the path of delusion, going straight to enlightenment.

NOTE 1

The original work used the place name Nishan (尼山) to refer to Confucius, because this is where he was born.

NOTE 2

That is, the theory of “cultivate yourself, maintain discipline, rule the country, and put peace in the world” is the basis of Confucius's doctrine of public order.

NOTE 3

The original work used the word Zhu Su (柱史) to refer to Lao Tzu, because according to the Tale of Cao Si (高士傳), the upper volume, the part about Lao Tzu Ly Nhi, he once held the position of royal historian in the Zhou court.

Duc Van Xuong Di Quan was a person who in many lifetimes always followed the five moral principles,4 reverence

NOTE 4

That is, the five principles of Confucianism, including: benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom and faith.

obey the teachings of the Three Teachings, use one's own merits to educate others, with only one heart to strive for goodness; Highly virtuous and bright, in charge of power, often worried about those who are uneducated, ignorant, ignorant and unaware of their eternal nature, so he wrote the essay Sound quality (陰騭文), which clearly states that he has "seventeen generations of birth as a scholar powerful". That essay has endless mysterious meanings. Who can measure its profound origin? Although many people have commented over the years, no one has fully grasped the profound depths of the text, causing up to now, those who teach and learn this literature still have some confusion and confusion, unable to fully understand it with satisfaction.

Mr. An Si is a person who has deeply planted the roots of blessings for many generations, following his good wish to be reborn in this world, understanding to the utmost of worldly books, penetrating deeply into the Buddhist scriptures, using that learning to teach and guide people, making everyone believe and accept it. He ventured into the worldly world to be a good model for people, using his knowledge of understanding and attaining miracles to grasp the essence of Buddhism as well as Taoism.1 followed the teachings of the Dharma according to Emperor Quan's background, including detailed comparative comments that are easy to understand for everyone.

NOTE 1

In the original work, the place names Linh Son (靈山) and Tu Thuy (泗 水) are used to refer to the birthplace of Zen Buddhism and Taoism.

covers the mind, clearly states the principle of meaning, raises the sun of wisdom to shine in the sky of true nature, making the reader have a place to learn after each incident, each thought has a place to self-admonish and repent; That is to directly communicate with the compassionate heart of Emperor Quan, to explain thoroughly, to clearly reveal the source, so that everyone in the world, those who teach and study this literature today, can understand everything clearly, without any confusion or entanglement.

But such compassion seems not enough, the great vow of love is still endless, he also wants everyone to develop a heart of sincerity and tolerance, to treat each other like brothers, to put an end to war and to enjoy life in peace, to use propriety as a precept, to love virtue and stay away from lust, so he immediately wrote a book to stop killing living things, named “Van Thien Tien Tu” (萬善先資), and another book to prevent indulging in lust, named “Desire sea of madness” (欲海回狂). It's only because people in this world have created too much killing karma, and when it comes to sexual immorality, it's easy to commit them. That's why Mr. was merciful, not afraid of hard work, and never stopped teaching.

However, good deeds in the world are nonetheless only rewarded in the two realms of heaven and human. After enjoying all the blessings, one must fall into the lower realms. How can one end the toxic suffering? That's why he read through the Sutras of the Pure Land sect, chose the appropriate words and compiled them into a book called “Western Guidance” (西歸直指), spreading it widely to help all people, whether rich or lowly, whether

old or young, men and women, whether wise or foolish, monks or lay people, all can recite the same thought. Amitābha Buddha, praying to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss, to escape the cycle of reincarnation, to ascend to a position of no more regression; End the suffering of illusory karma and enjoy the joy of the eternal mind.

The three books mentioned before,1 although clearly explain the method of practicing good worldly karma, but at the same time also have enough methods to understand life and death. The last volume2, although it clearly explains the Dharma of understanding life and death, at the same time teaches us to practice good karma in the world. Even things like "following the principles will bring good results, going against the principles will bring disaster", each of them is analyzed in detail, explained clearly, cleared up doubts, clarified ambiguities, the arguments are completely convincing, the language is wonderful and strange, can open the mind of a foolish person, and is strong enough to rescue a drowning person or save someone burned by fire. The most sincere place can be understood, consistent with the reasons in heaven and earth; Distinguishing the affairs of ghosts and gods, can eliminate doubts, and gain more prestige. The Six Classics,3 help define discipline from above and below. It is truly one of the most amazing books promoting good deeds in the world. If compared with other ordinary books promoting good deeds, can it be compared? I still firmly believe in my heart that he must be a Bodhisattva

NOTE 1

That means the three books Sound of Literature, Quang Nghia, Van Thien Tien Tu and Duc Hai Hoi Crazy.

NOTE 2

That is, the book of Western rules is direct.

NOTE 3

Six Classics: 6 essential ancient books of Confucianism, including the Poetry Sutra, the Thu Sutra, the I Ching, the Rites Sutra, the Music Sutra, and the Spring and Autumn Sutra. When talking about the Five Classics, we do not mention the Music Sutra.

according to the original vow, he appeared as a lay person to preach the Dharma to save sentient beings.

I was originally a poor person. Even though I read Confucian books when I was young, I did not understand the essence of Confucius's teachings. I have been studying Buddhism for a long time but still have not realized the Tathagata's nature. Time has passed, now we are about to enter the age of “tri heavenly mandate”1 but knowledge is shallow, only a heart that loves good deeds, there is really no energy to benefit others. I wanted to get this precious book engraved in large print, but I didn't know what to do. I was poor and had no land to support myself, and was lazy in calling for donations, so after many years my wish was still not fulfilled.

NOTE 1

That means nearly 50 years old, due to Confucius's saying "50 years old knows the destiny of heaven" (50 years old knows the destiny of heaven), so later people often use this idiom to refer to the age of fifty weeks.

There was a layperson from Tay Thuc land named Ly Thien Que, who had good roots, diligently cultivated good deeds, and hoped to attain the sublime Buddha Dharma. He came to worship at Phap Vu Pagoda on Putuo Mountain, so they met him by chance. Indeed:

If there is no predestined relationship,
Why don't we meet each other at the door of meditation?

He immediately respectfully asked, hoping to be shown the essence of the method of escaping samsara. I therefore advise you to first make an effort to keep the moral precepts, diligently practice pure karma, often do things that benefit yourself and others, following which is the most essential thing. If you can yourself

persist in practicing like this without interruption, you will surely be able to influence everyone around you. If one's own practice is not in accordance with the words spoken, then the transmission of the Dharma will turn out to be the opposite of destroying the Dharma. If worldly merit is not cultivated and accumulated, the good mind will not be transformed. Not cultivating merit and not transforming good hearts is all due to not meeting good teachers or friends to set a good example for us to follow.

On that occasion, I immediately brought out this book The Complete Book of An Si and gave him a copy, advising him to read it completely, paying attention to every single action every day according to the advice in the book, everything is compatible, without any deviation, it can be considered an achievement. That person was so happy as if he had received a treasure, his joy was endless, he immediately vowed to engrave and print it so it could be widely distributed everywhere, and asked me to write a foreword to announce to everyone.

Therefore, I am not afraid of poor learning, and briefly write down the reasons for the incident, with the desire to bring benefit to all people, so that everyone can improve themselves, build families, teach their children and grandchildren to follow the example of the sages, recognize the true nature of the heart, and thoroughly understand the truth of life and death. If anyone reads it carefully and tries to follow it, they will see exactly what I said, without any lies.

Like An Optical Mirror

FOREWORD BY TRUONG THU AN

On the occasion of reprinting

in the 7th year of Guangxu (1881)

I had never studied Buddhism before. That day, a guest came to visit and brought Mr. Chu An Si's Complete Books to show him. I opened the book and looked through a few parts, immediately showing frustration and not wanting to read anymore. The customer was surprised and asked: "Why do you have such an attitude?" I replied: "What Mr. An Si said here is completely contrary to the words of a man I know. Do you think that Mr. An Si's words are right, or must the other man's words be wrong?"

The guest laughed and said: "Your temper is so hot-tempered! Isn't this a matter of winning and losing? The argument between that gentleman and Mr. An Si is really not something that people like you and I can keep up with. I really don't dare to use the strength of a mayfly to try to shake the big tree, but do you want to use the fire of a firefly to burn down Mount Tu-di? Let's not discuss right or wrong, let's just talk about right now, for example. There are people who do not know about the next life, do not believe in cause and effect, so they aggressively do many evil things. There is another person who really knows that there is an afterlife,

believes in cause and effect, so he actively does many good deeds. So among those two, who do you think is better and who is worse? Having a nose but not being able to recognize scents?”

The guest immediately asked: “If that's the case, why do you doubt Mr. An Si's Complete Books?”

I replied: "Even though you are good at arguing, but if you follow the moral principles, you will be good, if you do contrary things, you will encounter bad things, or if you do good deeds, you will have joy, if you do many evil things, you will encounter disaster... then we Confucians have talked too much, why do we need to refer to Buddhist scriptures?"

The guest said: "It's just that you still haven't considered it carefully. Talking about reason." If we do not consider all three lives, past, present and future, we cannot be completely convincing. But it is only Buddha who can clearly explain cause and effect in the three lives. Therefore, Mr. An Si does not mind having people who are jealous, and warns the ignorant people to wake up class="book-paragraph">At that time, my heart gradually calmed down, and I smiled and replied: "That's because you only subjectively speculated and said it yourself. As expected, you hide your head and show your tail."

The guest immediately turned serious and said: "What that gentleman wrote is the dharma of the world, and what Mr. An Si wrote is a worldly dharma that is transparent to the dharma beyond the world. Every sentence and every word are words of passion and passion, like using a golden needle to open the eyes to help a blind person see light. I can't be more dedicated than that. Now the Complete Book is available here, if you go back and read it, you will definitely meet the teacher, there is no need for me to make so many lengthy explanations."

NOTE 1

Chinese medicine believes that the great doctors of the past were able to cure blindness by using a golden needle to penetrate the retina.

The customer said and then put the book back and gave it to me. I respectfully accepted it, opened it again and read it. At first, we still had to search for clues in the literary sentences, but gradually, we were able to grasp the meaning of the tone, suddenly awakening and understanding clearly. At that time, sadness and joy were mixed, like a lost person meeting a guide, like a serious illness encountering a good remedy, like a torch shining in the middle of a dark intersection, like an immense sea of suffering meeting a ship from the rescue, suddenly unable to hold back a sigh and lamenting: "Alas! If I hadn't been lucky enough to read this book, my life would have passed in vain!"

Thus, if I hadn't met a gentle friend like the old guest, Surely at the end of this life I will also

not know that there is a next life, nor will I believe that there is cause and effect.

Alas! Being human is difficult, listening to Buddha's teachings is even more difficult. Sentient beings suffer in the three evil paths,1 let's ask who caused it? Once upon a time, someone said: “Anyone who has ever drifted and wandered, must know how to sympathize and love the wanderers!”

NOTE 1

Three evil paths: hell, hungry ghosts and animals. Due to creating bad karma, one must be born in one of these 3 realms.

I write down the fate of reading this book, and send a message to those who later have the good fortune to encounter this book.

FIRST PREFACE OF THE BOOK EXTENDED LECTURES
TEXT
SOUND QUALITY

The I Ching says: “The house that often does good things will surely be rewarded. many good things.” The scripture writes: “Doing good deeds will result in hundreds of good things.” The book Ta Thi Xuan autumn1 also says: “The misfortunes and blessings are not predetermined by anyone, are only caused by people themselves.” So know that good deeds or disasters are natural in heaven and earth. The principles of the Three Teachings2 are not different, they are all the same. When the Confucianists heard that the theory of cause and effect was spoken by Buddhism, they immediately attributed things like following the good way, going against the bad way, cause and effect following each other like shadow and image, like echo and sound... all of it belongs to Buddhism. They also think that after death there is no next life, there is no retribution for doing good or evil... But if a person does not believe in cause and effect, there is nothing to be afraid of, in the end he probably just wants to be a petty person.

NOTE 1

Also called Ta Truyen, or Ta Thi Spring and Autumn Tale, written by Ta Khau Minh, it is called Ta Thi.

NOTE 2

Three religions: refers to Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism (ie Taoism).

Duc Van Xuong De Quan appeared in this world as a sage and saint to preach the Dharma, composed a poem of Sound quality to teach the readers of the book, from the very beginning he wrote: “I have spent seventeen generations being born as a scholar…” So it is clear that this life will definitely have a next life, and it will never end. Next, it was written: "If you keep a good heart like me, heaven will bless you", showing that good and evil things clearly have retribution, without the slightest deviation. At the end of the article, it is written: "Looking up to the ancient sages, carefully examining oneself not making mistakes; all evil deeds are determined not to do, all good deeds please obey." It is even more clearly shown, I have never seen anyone with a heart of love for life and saving people with such hard work, such sincerity and sincerity. Isn't it really a task that we Confucians can shoulder fully, without fear of ruining it?

Mr. Chu An Si read through all the books of the Three Teachings, selected the arguments of hundreds of schools, then brought out the essay The Sound of the Emperor by Wenchang Dijun, analyzed every sentence and every word thoroughly, included comments and annotations, very clear and transparent, and expanded on the interesting areas that were not complete, promoting mysterious meanings that had never been heard before, filtering out the trivial things. failed, unrealistic and untrue, decisively breaking away from short-sighted, limited knowledge, thus understanding more than 100,000 sentences, named Expanding the Essay on Sound Quality. Mr. Tieu Tung Hy read it and praised it with great interest. He only regretted that the engraving of the print was not even half finished. He immediately took the initiative to make a donation for this. Next, Mr. Co Tho Ky, Kim Nghieu Phong, La Doan Mai joined forces to support, brothers continued to work together and the work was achieved.

When the engraving was completed, Mr. Zhou wanted me to write a preface. I read this book and exclaimed: "You were able to mercifully use teachings to correct the mistakes of those who made mistakes, and you brothers were able to donate together to help do good things for people. Good hearts converge, making it even more glorious and beneficial. I only hope that those who have the good fortune to read this book will try their best to practice it themselves, aim for goodness and lead others forward together."

The golden words of Emperor1 cannot be allowed to fall into oblivion, it must be widely spread to all those who have a heart, not just limited to five or three gentlemen. I really have high hopes for this!

NOTE 1

The original work uses the word Yuanhuang (元皇) which is another name to refer to Emperor Wenchang.

Xunhua Tang Building2 inscription

NOTE 2

Duong Ton Hoa's (唐孫華) real name was Tru Quan (實君), nickname Dong Giang (東江), and in his old age took the title Tu Lu Lao Nhan (息廬老人). He was born in 1634, died in 1723, and received his doctorate in the 27th year of Kangxi (1688). Did you leave behind the Dong Giang exam book (東江詩鈔).

THE QUALITY ESSAY OF VAN XUONG DE QUAN
The Emperor said: “I have spent 17 generations as a powerful scholar, have never been tyrannical to the people, cruel to my subordinates; often save people in danger, help people in need, pity the lonely, tolerant If anyone can keep a good mind like me, he will be blessed by heaven.1 Therefore, I have this advice to everyone:

NOTE 1

Heaven bestows blessings: is an expression according to the theory of Heaven's Mandate or Heaven's predestination, which holds that all of each person's misfortunes and misfortunes are determined by heaven, which is a Confucian theory. However, when Buddhism was spread throughout China, those who studied Buddhism understood this theory in a slightly different way, that although all misfortunes and misfortunes were determined by heaven, it was not an arbitrary decision but based on the good and evil deeds each person had done. Understood in this way, "heaven" is only a representative of the principle of cause and effect, which according to Buddha's teachings operates on its own. Followers of Taoism (or Taoism) concretize this through the belief in recording each person's good and evil deeds in the Nam Tao book, so that the Jade Emperor can base on that to bestow blessings and disaster. It is the mixture of Confucianism - Buddhism - Laos like that that helps the theories of destiny and cause and effect to exist at the same time without contradicting each other.

In the past, Vu Cong took charge of the trial and built a large gate to wait for four-horse carriages; The Dau family helps many people, one root gives birth to five cinnamon branches; Tong Giao saved the ant colony and was elected to be a champion; Thuc Ngao buried the snake's body and later became prime minister.2 If you want to create a wide and deep field of blessings, you must rely on

NOTE 2

These stories were all excerpted by Great Master An Quang from ancient bibliographies and fully included in the supplement.

into this one heart; often constantly helping people, silently doing all kinds of merit; Benefit people, benefit animals, do good and accumulate merit. Righteousness replaces the heavens, teaches people, extends kindness, and saves the people for the country.

Be loyal to others, be filial to parents and grandparents; With brothers, we must maintain respect and love for each other; with friends, we must maintain trust. Either serve the true dynasty,1 or worship Buddha, study the sutras, and always remember to follow Buddha's teachings. Repaying the four profound graces,2 widely practice according to the Three Teachings.

NOTE 1

Worshiping the True Dynasty: Taoist belief that we must worship the true beings, worship the stars, believing that they are entrusted by the Jade Emperor to govern, teach, or reward and punish people.

NOTE 2

Four profound graces (Four great graces): Buddhist scriptures teach that each person has four profound graces to repay, including: 1. Grace to parents for giving birth and nurturing, also includes ancestors who passed down many generations to have our body; 2. Thanks to sentient beings for their mutual support and interaction, so that we can have the life we ​​have today, because everyone around us has a certain contribution to our life. It can also be understood more simply as thanks to the social community for giving us a good living environment; 3. Gratitude to the king, understood today, means those who take care of maintaining discipline and order in society, keeping our country peaceful, stable and developed; 4. Thanks to the Three Jewels, they have shown us the right path to follow, so that we can be good people, achieve peace and joy in life and move towards liberation from samsara. According to the book Thich Thi Tinh Su (釋氏要覽), the four heavy gratitudes of monastics are explained slightly differently, including: 1. Gratitude to parents; 2. Gratitude to ancestors and senior monks; 3. Gratitude to the king, the ruler of the country; 4. Gratitude to benefactors, those who provide for our practice. However, here we can also understand that gratitude to donors means gratitude to sentient beings as explained above, and gratitude to ancestors is also gratitude to the Three Jewels.Thus, these two explanations are similar and not contradictory.

Helping someone in an emergency is like a stranded fish; Rescue people in danger like birds caught in a net. Have pity on orphans and help widows; respect the elderly, love the poor; providing food, clothing and clothing for those who are hungry and cold on the road; Help the coffins of poor families so that the dead body can be warm. Wealthy people must support their relatives; When there is a bad season and famine, we have to help our neighbors. Weighing and measuring must be fair, not selling short and collecting old. With those below you, you must be tolerant, not harsh or critical.

Should contribute to widely printing and transmitting scriptures, building pagodas and monasteries. Helping people with medicine to cure suffering, water to quench their thirst. Either spend money to buy living animals to release animals, or become vegetarian and abstain from killing. Every time you take a step, you must pay attention to avoid trampling insects; Do not light fires that cause forest fires or mountain fires. Dark nights help pedestrians have lights; Wide rivers help boats carry people back and forth. Do not use nets to catch birds and animals on land, do not use poison to catch fish and shrimp in the water.1 Do not kill buffaloes; Do not throw away paper with writing on it. Do not scheme to take other people's property; Don't be jealous of people with technical talent. Do not indulge in evil thoughts with other people's wives. Do not incite people to litigate. Don't ruin other people's fame and fortune, don't break up other people's marriages. It is not because of personal hatred that causes discord between brothers; not for the sake of a little profit, but to make the father and son different from each other

NOTE 1

Although they are also killing animals, these two forms are much more cruel than other forms of hunting, because by spreading nets, birds and animals of all species are caught, and by drugging, large and small fish and shrimp are killed. By fishing like this, all things on land and in the water are quickly depleted, and the environment is also damaged and cannot be easily restored.

becomes incompatible. Do not rely on power to humiliate good people; Do not rely on wealth and despise the poor.

When meeting good people, we must be close and close, because they can help us increase the goodness of the mind and the goodness of the body. If you encounter evil people, you must stay away immediately, because in just a blink of an eye, they can bring us unimaginable disasters. We must often practice to eliminate evil and promote good deeds; When you speak true words with your mouth, you must not think wrong things in your heart. Clear thorns and bushes that block the road, clear rocks and bricks blocking the path. Roads that have been bumpy for many years need to help repair and level them; The river is wide and thousands of people often cross it, so they work hard to build a bridge.

Use love to teach and correct people's mistakes. Donating money helps people achieve good things. Whatever you do, follow the way of heaven, and whatever you say will be in accordance with people's hearts. Admiring the sages and sages, even when walking, standing, lying or sitting, I still think about them; Be careful to maintain your dignity so that when you are alone, you will not feel anything to be ashamed of. Do not do all evil deeds, please obey all good deeds.

Eternally does not encounter bad omens, and is often helped by good spirits. Blessings that are close to you are enjoyed by yourself, but far away they affect your children and grandchildren. Hundreds of blessings come at the same time, thousands of good things converge. Isn't that possible thanks to the accumulation of negative virtue?

noi_dung:
ADDITIONS

Mr. An Si compiled this book, from the arguments, events to meaningful literature, everything is complete and thoughtful. However, there are 5 notable events:

1. Emperor Quan's final incarnation 2. Vu Cong kept the trial 3. Thi Dau helps many people 4. Song Giao saves ants 5. Thuc Ngao buries the snake's body

When examining these stories, either because there are stories that have never been officially recorded, or because there are stories that have been fully published in other books, people of later generations are well aware of them, so they should be omitted.

However, like that, people who have never read many books probably cannot know these stories. This is truly a very unfortunate thing for the future. Therefore, now based on the annotations and evidence of the essay Sound Quality to add the above stories to this printed version, making the truth clear.

But it's just copied verbatim, without any changes.

Thich An Quang Kinh recorded

The last incarnation of Emperor Quan

Di Quan was born in the Jin Dynasty,1 surnamed Truong, first name A, his ancestors were originally from Vietnam, later moved to Shu, living in Tu Dong (Sichuan). He grew up handsome and elegant, with a generous and generous personality, brilliant literature, clear and open, and became a master in the land of Shu. Feeling moved by the unstable times at that time, he set out to travel far away. Later, the disciples who had studied together built a temple to worship him, naming him Van Xuong Quan.

NOTE 1

The Jin dynasty lasted from 266 to 420, divided into two periods: Western Jin (266-316) and Eastern Jin (317-420). The following section states more clearly that Emperor Quan was born in 287, near the end of the Western Jin period.

During the Tang Dynasty, two kings, Duong Huyen Tong2 and Duong Hy Tong3, while avoiding the rebels and fleeing into Shu, were protected and helped by him. When the enemy calmed down, the king came down to promulgate him as King of Tan.4 Later generations honored him as Emperor, all because of their respect for him.

NOTE 2

Emperor Xuanzong reigned from 712 to 756, met with An Lushan rebellion in 755.

NOTE 3

Emperor Xuanzong reigned from 873 to 888, met Huang Chao rebelled around 874. Around the end of 880, he had to leave the capital Chang'an and flee to Chengdu, and did not return to Chang'an until 885. In 886, he encountered internal turmoil again among the generals and had to leave Truong An and flee to Hung Nguyen. In 888, he returned to Truong An and died after only a month.

NOTE 4

The two kings lived centuries apart, and here it is not clearly stated which king was crowned king. However, considering that if Huyen Tong already had a decree, then Hy Tong would have had to inherit the throne, so the decree granting the title of King of Tan was probably from Duong Hy Tong.

Vu Cong tried the case, built a large gate to wait for four carriages horses

Vu Cong was born during the Han Dynasty, was from Dong Hai district,1 held the position The official oversees the trial in the district. Dong Hai district has a widow who is extremely filial, determined to live alone, worship her husband, and take care of her mother-in-law very attentively. The mother-in-law felt sorry for her and was afraid that she would hinder her daughter-in-law's remarriage, so she hanged herself. Her daughter falsely accused her daughter-in-law of forcing her mother-in-law to death. The widow could not defend herself.

NOTE 1

Belongs to Tan district, today Tan Thanh, Shandong province. The way China divided administrative boundaries at that time was that each province was divided into districts, and each district was divided into districts.

Vu Cong knew that the case was unjust and tried his best to protect him, but the governor at that time did not listen. The widow was sentenced to death. Immediately after that, Dong Hai district suffered from drought for 3 years.

When a new mandarin came to replace him, Vu Cong brought up the unjust case. The governor asked him to go to the grave of the unjustly filial widow and make offerings. Immediately after that it rained heavily.

Vu Cong worked, and every time he made an opinion or judgment, the people respectfully followed him. The main gate of his house collapsed, so the elders and relatives gathered to discuss rebuilding it. Vu Cong said: "We should make a gate so that four-horse carriages can pass through in the future.1 I keep the trial, I have accumulated a lot of negative virtue, I have never made an unjust decision, my future descendants must prosper."

NOTE 1

A carriage pulled by four horses is a large carriage, in the past only high-ranking officials and powerful people could have it. At that time, Vu Cong's family did not have a four-horse carriage, but he believed that he had done many good deeds, benefited the people, and accumulated good virtue, so his future descendants would certainly be prosperous like that.

Afterwards, his son made great contributions to the country, and indeed reached the position of Prime Minister, was awarded the title of Binh Tay Marquis, and his descendants were passed down to hold the position of Royal Palace Master.

The Dau family helped many people, a person born in the year of cinnamon branches

During the Five Dynasties,2 Dau Vu Quan from Yen Son,3 was over 30 years old but had no children. One day, I dreamed that my deceased grandfather appeared and taught: "Not only do you have no children, but you will also have a short life. You should soon cultivate your merits and pray for the fate of heaven."

NOTE 2

Here refers to the Later Zhou period, the Five Dynasties of China at that time including the Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han and Later Zhou dynasties.

NOTE 3

Now belongs to Mat Van district, He Bac province.

Dau Vu Quan tried his best to do many good deeds because of that. A maid in the house stole two hundred thousand dong from him. When things broke out, he immediately wrote a note to sell his little daughter to compensate. The paper said: "I sell this daughter forever to compensate for the debt." Later, this person

ran away again. Dau Vu Quan took pity on her, immediately burned the debt papers, adopted her daughter, and when she grew up, she carefully took care of choosing where to get married. For those who had relatives, whether they were in mourning or were too poor to take care of them, he paid money to help with the funeral; If anyone has a daughter who doesn't have enough money to get married, he will also help out.

He calculates his income each year, keeps just enough for expenses, and gives whatever is left to help others. Family life is very frugal, no gold or jewelry, no concubines or concubines. He set up a library in the south corner of his house, collected more than a thousand books, then invited teachers to open classes for orphaned or poor students everywhere, providing all their educational needs. Many people asked him for help like that and later became enlightened.

Soon, he gave birth to five sons in a row, all of whom were intelligent and handsome. After that, he dreamed that his grandfather appeared and said: "For many years now, you have done great meritorious deeds. Your name is now recorded in the book of heaven, you will live another 3 centuries.1 All five of your children will be honored. You should try to do more good deeds, not be lazy and lose your good heart."

UNCUSED LIKE 1

According to the old way of calculating, each era is 12 years, so 3 eras are 36 years.

Later, his eldest son Dau Nghi became

the position of Minister of Rites. The second son, Dau Nghiem, worked for the Ceremony of Thi Lang. The third son, Dau Khan, became mandarin Ta Bo Quyet. The fourth son, Dau Xunh, became the Ta Gian Nghi Dai Doc, and was able to participate in important political affairs. The fifth son, Dau Hy, became mandarin Khoi Cu Lang. The eight grandchildren later also received glory and wealth.

He lived to be 82 years old. One day he was not sick. While chatting and laughing with his relatives, he suddenly passed away peacefully.

The famous scholar of that time, Phung Dao, had a poem dedicated to him as follows:

燕山竇十郎,
敎子有義方。
靈椿一株老,
丹桂五枝芳。

Yen Son Dau Thap Lang,
The right teacher.

Temporarily translated:

Yen Son has Dau Vu Quan,
Teaching children according to morality and kindness,
A good father has a majestic root,
Gives birth to a glorious child with five fragrant cinnamon branches.1

NOTE 1

Because of this legend, later generations often use "five cinnamon branches" to refer to accumulating virtue and giving birth to glorious descendants.

Song Giao saved ants, was elected to become a poet

During the Song Dynasty, there were two brothers, Tong Giao and Tong Ky. One day while sitting together reading a book, a monk saw him, looked at his appearance and said: "The younger brother will win the prestigious award, the older brother will also pass high."

The following spring, that monk met again and happily told his older brother, Tong Giao, "You must have saved hundreds of thousands of lives!" Tong Giao laughed and said: "I'm a poor student, I don't have the strength to do such a thing!"

The monk said: "That's right. Because of this, this year my brother still won the title, but in the end I can't lose him."

When the exam results were announced, Tong Ky indeed passed the position. The court drew up a program for the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother took a look and thought that she could not be placed above him, so she wrote and edited Song Giao's article to be number one, and Song Ky's name was added from number one (一) to become number ten (十).

At that time, I realized that what the monk said was indeed not wrong.

Thuc Ngao buried snakes, later became Prime Minister

Sun Thuc Ngao was from the country of Chu. When he was young, he often went out here and there. One day he saw a snake with two heads, so he killed it and buried it. When I got home, I was so worried that I stopped eating. The mother asked about the matter, Thuc Ngao cried and said: "I heard people say that whoever sees a two-headed snake must die. Today I saw it, and I was afraid that I would die and leave my mother."

The mother asked: "Where is that snake now?"

Thuc Ngao replied: "I was afraid that someone else would see that it was harmful, so I killed it and buried it."

The mother said: "Don't worry, I heard that people who do deeds that accumulate positive virtue will receive good retribution. You will surely be prosperous in this land of So in the future."

Sure enough, Ton Thuc Ngao later issued an Order. Doan,1 held the government of So.

NOTE 1

The position of Commander Doan of the State of Chu is equivalent to the Prime Minister, who is the top official in the court.

QUAN THUONG

Kunshan Chu Mong Title of An Si before narrative

Translated and annotated by Nguyen Minh Tien Viet

I HAVE EXPERIENCED SEVENTEEN LIFE Born as a scholar with the right to do so
THIS

Preach widely

- MUST BELIEVE IN THE AFTER LIFE1

NOTE 1

We have added some small topics for readers to follow.

Tin this article, all are the words of the Lord Emperor incarnate and preach the Dharma, so we should refer to it as “I” to opening. Saying "through seventeen lives" means specifically wanting to bring out the original part hidden in this so-called "my body", from ancient times to the present, through many lifetimes of birth and death, it has never been damaged, and clearly pointed it out for future people to know.

People in this world just because they are born without knowing where they come from, and when they die they don't know where they are going, so they think that when they die, their body and mind will end, and there will be no afterlife. Therefore, let go of all actions, without any hesitation or fear. Because Emperor Quan was extremely afraid of such deluded people, making mistakes themselves and then leading others to make mistakes, causing that toxic delusion to never end, he officially made it clear to everyone about his own story that had "experienced seventeen generations". If you do not do good deeds and think that you will receive blessings in the next life, it is impossible.

- I AM THE HOST, THE BODY IS THE GUEST

People in the world read scriptures, often because their mind is crude, their mind is wandering, so they cannot consider deeply and naturally

comprehend. Regarding the concept of names such as "body" and "me", it is often impossible not to fall into confusion and confusion. If we can clearly realize that "body" can refer to "me" but "I" cannot refer to "body", then we can understand that "I" is the owner, and "body" is only a temporary guest. Being a "master" will of course last forever, without birth or death; Being a "temporary guest" must come and go, changing shape.

For example, a person going far away, sometimes rowing a boat, sometimes sitting in a palanquin, sometimes riding a horse, sometimes driving... vehicles change in all kinds of ways, but the person never changes. Boats, palanquins, horses, carriages... those are the body, the guests, and the person rowing the boat, sitting on the palanquin, riding the horse, driving the car, that is me, the owner.

For example, if a person is assigned a role to play, sometimes he pretends to be a king, sometimes he pretends to be a mandarin, and sometimes he pretends to be a beggar... often changing his appearance, but the real person does not change. Kings, mandarins, beggars... these are relatives, guests; The person who plays the role of king, mandarin, beggar... is me, the boss.

If we only take this present body, then the ability to "see images and hear sounds" belongs to the body, the guest, and the person who "sees images and hears sounds" is us, the owner. Because the body has birth and death, as we get older, our eyes gradually become blurry and our ears gradually become deaf. I am the master, truly without birth and death, so even though the eyes are dim, the person seeing is not dim, the ears are deaf, but the person hearing is not deaf. Therefore, it is decided that:

If I speak, I see, I hear,

Is it no different from accepting an enemy into your home as your child?

Therefore, people with wisdom based on the great nature can use this temporary fake body as a means of practice. On the contrary, the deluded person obscures his own nature, becomes narrow, loses his master position, and is always controlled by this temporary false body.

- LIVING AND DEATH THROUGH MANY LIVES

If there have been 17 lifetimes, there can be 70 lifetimes, 70 lifetimes, then there can also be countless countless lifetimes. Thus, the "I" of the Emperor mentioned here is infinite, and the "I" of all of us is also infinite. And if the Emperor can be born as a "scholar", as a "great doctor", then he can also be born as a heavenly body, a dragon body... in the eight classes, 1 can also be born as a body in the realms of hell, hungry ghosts... As the Emperor's body is not certain, then the bodies of all of us are also not certain.

The story of the past life and the next life is like day after day, the sun rises and sets; That sentient beings are immersed in samsara, which is such a truth, does not come from Buddhism at all. For example, all internal organs are available in the patient's body, so why not just because you hear those names spoken from the doctor's mouth and think that those things must be in the medicine basket?

If people really don't have an afterlife or reincarnation, there must be a lot of discontent in the world, and all the treatises of the saints and sages don't have enough evidence to believe. heaven and hell are just myths and fabrications, past lives and next lives are so vague and obscure that it is impossible to know, that when this body is born, it has nothing to do with the previous one, and when it dies, it leaves no trace. If you leave this body and do not take on another body, then that is a "death" that will forever be gone, a "death" that will forever be gone. Calmly examine yourself and ask those two words "death", in the end, who is the recipient? Alas! Holding a knife to kill someone, however, it can only cut into human flesh. To say that there is no afterlife is to cut off the intellectual life of others. Slashing the flesh only harms this one life, but cutting off the intellectual base is killing people for many lives. Therefore, we must know that,

advising people to abandon evil and do good is a secondary matter, but first it is necessary to justify and clarify that if there is this life, there must be a next life, that is the most essential basis.

If an evil person were to say the rebuttal that there is no afterlife, everyone who would listen would ignore it with disdain. Just like someone who wants to harm people but puts poison in food that already smells rancid, few people will eat it, so the harm is insignificant.

Like a person who has the ability to argue clearly and firmly, with a heart that saves people and helps the world, and is determined not to follow such words, he will certainly gain great merit.

happiness, harming others is harming themselves, surely in the darkness and darkness, they will naturally start trembling in fear of evil deeds, and love to do good deeds. 3. ARE SAINTS DIFFERENT FROM MORTAL PEOPLE?

Question: The loyal and filial servants of the past, of course, have not been lost for a thousand years, so there is no doubt about the Emperor's reincarnation for more than seventeen generations. But for ordinary people with ordinary temperaments, once they die, their soul will surely dissipate, how can it still exist forever?

Answer: The form is big or small, smart or stupid, but the true nature is not big or small, smart or stupid. If you think that after death, ordinary people will completely disappear, try asking when the Emperor died in Cung Tri, but he was just a snake. If according to that theory, it must have been destroyed, how can there still be a Emperor in the future?

4. WHY DO SOMEONE SAY THAT AFTER DEATH THE CONSCIOUSNESS IS DISAPPEARED?

Question: Looking through the records of many dynasties, one can believe that there really is a story of reincarnation through many lifetimes, but recently, looking at Chu Hy's book Primary School, it was said: After a person dies, when the body is damaged, the soul also disappears. Therefore, there should be some doubts?

Answer: That Primary Book also quotes Pham

Van Chanh,1 as saying: Those who only know how to enjoy wealth and wealth for themselves but do not know how to share and help their clan members, will not be able to see the faces of their ancestors in the underworld in the future. Is that what Chu Hy wrote down?

All of these things clearly show that the consciousness of the previous predecessors did not dissipate or disappear. If you think that the words of the ancient Confucian sages are trustworthy, then the words of Yao, Shun, Zhou, and Confucius are much more trustworthy. And if it is said that the words of Yao, Shun, Zhou, and Confucius are not trustworthy enough, then why are they still handed down by the Confucian sages of the past?

What's more, if we think that the dead people's consciousness is truly dissipated and destroyed, surely the Confucian sages of the past, although many, must now be among those who are destroyed and destroyed. So why is there a need for two ceremonies each year, spring and autumn? If today we still carry out annual sacrifices in the spring and autumn seasons, then the theory of spiritual destruction will not be believed by future generations, so what will be needed to convince future generations?

Mencius, when reading Thien Vu Thanh in the Kinh Thu, only selectively believed a few parts of it, let alone Chu Hy's book Primary Education!

5. HOW CAN A HUMAN BE REINCARNED AS ANIMALS?

Question: Such consciousness will not be destroyed, it will return and be reborn. Now I have heard stories about life like that, but if it is said that dead people turn into animals, and animals can be reincarnated as humans, I don't believe that.

Answer: Forms inherently change depending on consciousness. A benevolent thought means being the same in the realm of heaven and man. A cruel thought, the seed of demons and animals, has begun to sprout. Good and bad actions interact with each other without being consistent. Of course, the two realms of humans and animals also change and change without being fixed. If we say that if we are human, we will always be human, and animals will always be animals, then right at the beginning of dividing humans and animals, isn't it too unfair?

Someone asked a monk: "Why does the human body walk upright, but the animal body must walk horizontally?" The monk replied: "To be born as a human means that in the previous life the mind was upright and upright, so in this life the body stands upright and walks. To be born as an animal means that in the previous life the mind was not upright and straight, so in this life the body must walk horizontally."

If the mind is upright or not upright, it changes in every moment, so the body also changes accordingly, being born as a human today, born tomorrow as an animal, isn't that just crazy impermanence?

Only humans have shame, so they know how to use clothes. Animals do not know shame or shyness, so they do not use clothes. Humans, thanks to blessings, know how to change and wear different appropriate clothes during the two hot and cold seasons, while animals, due to lack of blessings, only know how to endure the two seasons of heat and cold with their existing fur.

Furthermore, to be born as a human means that in the previous life, one often speaks words of kindness, words of benefit, words of sincerity, words of respect and faith in the Three Jewels, so in this life, depending on the mind's manifestations, the mouth can say all kinds of things; Being born as an animal means that in your previous life, you often said cruel words, lies, probing words, prying into other people's private affairs, gossiping, dirty and dirty words, slandering Buddha, slandering the Dharma, not believing in cause and effect. Therefore, in this life, even though you have a mouth, you cannot speak, even if you are hungry and thirsty, you cannot open your mouth to ask for help. tieu_de: He has never been tyrannical to his people or cruel to his subordinates
noi_dung:
NEVER BE VIOLENT TO CEOPLE, CRUEL TO SUBJECTS

Preach widely

From this sentence to the previous sentence “deep into the heart "Heaven", are all words told by Emperor Quan himself about his merits in the past 17 lives, to serve as a basis for the teachings below.

The next six sentences mean, having done it yourself

only then advising others to do the same. In particular, the sentence "never tyrannical to the people, cruel harsh to subordinates" means: If you cannot do it yourself, then there is no way others can imitate it.

A mandarin is recognized by the people as a father and mother, considered the father and mother of the people, if he treats the people tyrannically, it is inhumane. All subordinate officials are concerned with serving and helping us, no different from serving the king or a superior mandarin. If we treat them cruelly, it is unrighteous.

When talking about tyranny, it doesn't necessarily mean strict laws or too strict regulations, but it can be things like when collecting taxes and land taxes from the people, being forced and forced unreasonable; or arbitrarily increase the list to collect surplus; or when a natural disaster occurs such as drought or crop failure, it is not reported in time to provide relief to the people; Or when people have injustices, they request them to hide them and keep them quiet without reporting them; or deciding on cases, deciding on imprisonment without carefully listening to the common people and hastily condemning; or mistrial involving too many innocent people; or a small event that is exaggerated or exaggerated into a big, important event; Or instead of ending on time, it drags on for many days later. All such things, according to the Emperor's teachings, can be considered tyranny against the people.

Talking about cruelty, it does not necessarily mean freely using whips and staffs to beat and torture, but

can be things like punishing small mistakes; or personnel make mistakes or unintentional mistakes and reprimand them; or influenced by emotions of joy and anger, treating people differently is unfair; or believe in false flattery and arbitrarily reward and punish here and there, unfair to subordinates; or when going far away, using too many people to serve and serve; or rule others without caring about their hunger, cold or deprivation. All such things, according to the Emperor's teachings, can be considered cruel to his subordinates.

Alas! When you hold power and a title but don't know how to use it as a means to benefit the people, it's like entering a treasure trove but returning empty-handed! In the past seventeen generations, the Emperor has never been cruel to his people or cruel to his subordinates!

Citing legends

His subordinates and servants who made even the slightest mistake were subjected to whipping punishments at his discretion. He came

each sentence is a straightforward admonition, like an antidote.
