tieu_de: Save people in times of danger
noi_dung:
SAVING PEOPLE IN DANGEROUS TIME

Extensive preaching

Danger comes in many forms, but to summarize, there are only seven things: one is flood, two is fire, three is unjust imprisonment. waste, four is robbery, five is war, six is crop failure and famine, seven is infectious disease.

When you meet someone in flood or fire, you can find a way to preserve their life, that is called rescuing. When you meet a person who has been unjustly imprisoned, you can find a way to help the exonerated person, which is called rescuing. When you encounter someone who is suffering from robbery, fire or war, you can find a way to help them escape safely, which is called rescuing. Encountering people who are hungry and cold because of crop failures, being able to help them with food and clothing is called rescuing them. When you encounter someone suffering from an epidemic, you can use medicine to treat it, which is called helping.

All of that help must come from a sincere heart, seeing the victim also

I thought I was in trouble, so I devoted all my energy and intelligence to find every way to help, so that he could completely escape the disaster.

When a person is in trouble and then comes to help, that is visible help, as Confucius said: “If a person is in trouble, he must put himself in the other person's situation to help.” There is another method, which makes people naturally not encounter danger. Helping in this way has much greater merit, as Confucius said: “Keeping people from facing danger.”

What does that mean? That's because people who encounter hardships are all created by previous karma. In this life, if you don't sow bad causes, in the next life you will naturally not experience bad results. If we can advise people not to commit the karma of killing, stealing, adultery, and cheating, that will save them from many dangers. Therefore, saving people when the danger has already occurred is limited, but saving people when the danger has not yet occurred is infinite.

Saving people when they are in trouble is a good deed for ordinary people; Saving people by teaching them so that they never have to encounter suffering is the virtue of Bodhisattvas. Both of these things can be done at the same time, and are not contradictory.

Citing the story

CLARIFYING A STRANGE INJURY CASE

Di Quan said: There was a man named Ha Chi Thanh who lived at the foot of Quy Son mountain, gave birth to two sons, named the eldest son Ha Vo Phuong, the second son Ha Luong Nang.

The eldest son grew up and married the daughter of the Marquis. After a year, the Marquis became ill, so the girl asked to visit, and when she returned, she went with her husband. I was so confused that when I left I forgot my dowry jade bracelet. When he suddenly remembered and was still wondering what to do, Ha Luong Nang chased after him with a jade bracelet and said, "Mom is also sick, I hope you come back soon." Hearing this, Ha Vo Phuong told his younger sister to protect her sister-in-law on the way home, and even rushed back to visit her sick mother.

After walking a while, the sister-in-law felt shy and told her brother-in-law: "My house is not far, I don't dare bother you with the effort of following." Therefore, Luong Nang immediately returned home.

That night, the Hau family waited forever but did not see their daughter return. In the morning, I followed the road and found a girl's body lying dead, her head cut off. Hau Phu was so heartbroken that he passed away. The Hau family suspected that Luong Nang wanted to rape his sister-in-law and killed her because she did not comply. They immediately filed a complaint with the government. Luong Nang was tortured and forced to confess and couldn't bear it. In the end, he had to confess his crime and was sentenced to death.

At that time, the mountain god Quy Son, Ngai Man, reported that injustice, and I immediately looked into the matter. It turned out that that night, there was a violent robber named Nguu Tu, and his wife Mao Thi had an argument, and in anger, he accidentally killed his wife. At that time, he happened to meet the daughter of the Hau family walking alone on the road, immediately captured her and raped her, and swapped her clothes with Mao's corpse. Thi Mao and Hau Thi were almost the same age, so they had similar bodies. Niu Tu immediately cut off Mrs. Mao's head and hid it, took the body and threw it on the side of the road, then took Marquis and brought it back to his house, no one knew about it.

I immediately searched for Mao's soul, made her temporarily enter Niu Tu's body, and used Niu Tu's own mouth to tell what happened to her. The government official heard the truth clearly and ordered Nguu Tu to be beheaded at the market. The Hau family's daughter was returned home, and Ha Luong Nang's injustice was cleared up.

Discussion

Mortal people can only see the external appearance of people, but demons can see through the heart. Therefore, the laws of the earthly world can be unjust, but the blame in the invisible cannot escape.

EXTRACT RUINS, SAVE GENTLE PEOPLE

Di Quan said: In Bac Quach village, there was a rich man named Tri Toan Le. On the occasion of Trong Xuan festival, a sacrifice ceremony was held, after which the whole family, big and small, drank until they were drunk. There was a violent robber named Vuong Tai who led his accomplices to rob the Tri family, tying up a total of 9 men and women, and 7 more concubines. Only Toan Le's wife and two daughters, Thuan Anh and Thuan Hoa, were not tied up yet. The two girls hugged their mother and cried. Vuong Tai wanted to rape her, so her younger sister loudly scolded her: "You hungry invaders dare to rob my house. Truong, the god, already knows your crime."

As soon as I finished speaking, the family god along with the ancestors of the Tri family came together to report to me. I immediately sent Cong Tao to lead hundreds of soldiers to rescue. At that moment, Toan Le and everyone in the house suddenly saw the ropes untie themselves, so they rushed out together to arrest all the robbers and tie them up. When the government heard about the army coming, they immediately arrested all of them and punished them.

Discussion

The reason Vuong Tai dared to rob was because all the family members were drunk and had no strength to resist. And Toan Le's whole family was drunk, because they drank too much before having fun. For example, if the homeowner knows how to stay alert and not get confused, surely everyone in the house, big and small, can also maintain vigilance, so they don't have to bring disaster from outside?

Very scary! The head of the family cannot help but always stay alert! If a person does not have true wisdom and correct understanding, he or she will be robbed of all the treasures in his house by the six thieves who specialize in stealing merit, which are the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind.

tieu_de: Help people when in need
noi_dung:
HELP PEOPLE IN EMERGENCY

Broadening

The cases called urgent are not the same as the cases called dangerous. We often say danger to refer to unexpected unfortunate events, but urgency usually refers to cases of too much material deprivation.

People in everyday life consider money as life, that is, they want to keep in life from lack of food and clothing, when they are sick, they do not lack medicine, these are all urgent things. If a family has a son or daughter who has reached adulthood, it is urgent to arrange marriage. If someone dies in the house, the funeral of the coffin is urgent. Depending on your ability and strength, in those urgent situations you can support and assist others in overcoming it, that is called helping others.

Confucius said: "If you practice the great religion, you will be a person of the whole world. Therefore, you should not only love your own relatives, not only be filial and respectful to your parents."

Also said: "Regarding wealth, hating waste and throwing it away, it is not necessary to keep it as one's own. If you have strength, hate laziness and not working hard, nor necessarily working only for yourself. 1

NOTE 1

These words of Confucius are taken from the book of Rites in the Rites Book.

If you sincerely understand and understand the above words, even though the urgent need is in someone else, you will not be able to consider it as someone else's problem, but will accept it as your own. If we can consider other people's urgent need as our own, then in life after life, we will never be in a needy situation again.

Mr. Tran Ky Dang said: "People call a rich person a tycoon, meaning that he can be the owner and knows how to use his assets ethically." Although your family career still needs to develop, you should also know how to help and provide for others according to your strength. Nowadays, people who have a lot of property often become slaves to that property. Being able to accumulate assets and being able to use assets at will is worthy of being called a wealthy person. If you only know how to accumulate a lot of assets but cannot use them at will, then you should only be called a slave, that is, a slave of assets.

The Upasaka Sutra teaches that: "If you give clothes to others, you will have a beautiful and wonderful appearance one day; if you give food to others, you will gain infinite strength the next day; if you help others with means of enlightenment, you yourself will have miraculous clear and bright eyes; if you help others with means of transportation, you yourself will be happy; if you help others have a safe place to live, you yourself will always be complete." no hunger.”1

NOTE 1

This excerpt begins from line 5, page 1059, page a, volume 5 of the Upasaka Precepts Sutra (優婆塞戒經). In total, this sutra has 7 volumes, classified in the Dai Chanh modernized Tripitaka in volume 24, sutra number 1488, translated by Mr. Dam Vo Sam in the Northern Luongng period.

It also teaches that: “If you help others with needs such as food, clothing, housing... with a heart of love and joy, you will gain immeasurable merit and virtue. measure.”2

NOTE 2

This excerpt starts from line 19, page 1059, page a of the sutra just cited above.

Citing the story

POVER AND RICH IN JUST A MOMENT

Di Quan said: When Emperor Shu had just ascended the throne, that year the crops were lost, severe famine spread everywhere, especially in Ba Tay district, it was even more serious. There was a rich farmer, La Mat, who had accumulated more than five thousand buckets of rice. 3 closed the warehouse door and kept it tight, refusing to sell it. There is another person full of chivalry, Hua

NOTE 3

Box: an ancient unit of measurement, equal to 10 measures, each measure equivalent to about 5 liters.

Dung, devote all your resources to help the poor. When he could no longer help anymore, he burned incense all night and prayed to heaven for help. The god in the district, Lai Hoa Ton, reported this matter to me.

I reported to the Jade Emperor, who issued a decree to collect the rice in La Mat's house and distribute it to save the poor people. I immediately ordered the wind god to blow up La Mat's house, causing all the rice bags inside to be blown away by the wind, then fall from the air everywhere, gathering themselves into piles. Everyone in the district has enough to eat. As for the La family, all their accumulated assets were lost in just one day. People in the district were grateful to Hua Dung for helping him before, so many people brought rice to repay him.

That's also because the La family sees people in disaster but stands by gloating and doesn't try to help. At that time, Emperor Thuc appointed Hua Dung as district colonel.1 When La Mat heard about it, he felt so ashamed that he hanged himself and died.

NOTE 1

District colonel: auxiliary official position, assistant to the district command.

Discussion

This is called magical powers. The story of making rice rain from the sky, although it was the Emperor's report, but this way of joking and joking with people, in fact, the heavens often do it. We would like to record here the story of wealthy man Lo Chi in the past for readers to conveniently refer to.

In ancient India, there was a wealthy businessman, Lo Chi, who was extremely rich but extremely stingy and miserly. His wife, children, and servants all suffered because of his stinginess. One fine day, Lo Chi sneaked four coins to buy wine and meat, took it out to a deserted cemetery, and ate and drank alone. But Lo Chi was not used to drinking alcohol, so as soon as he drank, he got drunk. While drunk and in high spirits, he sang a song saying:

Now I have all the luck,
Sipping delicious wine is extremely pleasurable.
More truly than King Bhikkhu,1

NOTE 1

Bhikkhu Thien Vuong, is the Heavenly King in this realm, his palace is located about halfway up Mount Tu-di.

Exceeding even the heavenly king Indra.2

NOTE 2

The heavenly king Indra (Thien De Thich), is the Heavenly King in the Dao Loi heaven.

At that time, De Thich heard the song, burst out laughing and said: "This person's food is only worth four coins, yet he dares to say that it is more pleasurable than mine. I have to find a way to disturb him."

Thinking so, he transformed like Lo Chi, appeared at his house and called all the people in the house to say: "I have always treated you very badly. I was born like that because I was haunted by a stingy demon. Today, while I was out playing, I was able to escape it. Now, if you all need anything in this house, please use it as you please." Having said that, he immediately opened the warehouse door, distributed everything to everyone, and again

said: "That stingy demon has the same shape as me, in a moment it will come. You must chase it away, if you let it into the house, it will enter and make me become stingy again like before."

Everyone in the house obediently listened. Suddenly seeing Lo Chi returning sober, the doorkeeper immediately chased him away and did not let him in. Lo Chi loudly called his wife and children. It turned out that even his wife and children came out with sticks and sticks to chase him away. Lo Chi was extremely frightened, so he went to his close friends to cry and tell the story. Those friends immediately came together to take him home. Lo Chi's wife and children saw it and said: "No, he is a stingy devil, why do you believe his words?"

A few friends looked into the house and saw De Thich pretending to be Lo Chi, thinking that Lo Chi was indeed still in the house, then turned and scolded Lo Chi: "You are a stingy devil, how dare you deceive us."

Lo Chi at that time had a speechless mouth and could hardly make excuses, so he managed to borrow a piece of silk cloth from an acquaintance, intending to present it to the king to tell the story of his injustice.1 The doorkeeper did not accept or let him in, so Lo Chi shouted loudly: "I want to offer property, I want to offer property." The king heard it and told him to come in.

NOTE 1

According to the regulations at that time, people who wanted to sue or complain had to first offer a piece of silk cloth to add to the public fund.

Lo Chi entered the palace and just wanted to offer a piece of silk cloth to complain, suddenly his armpits closed tightly to hold the piece of silk cloth. Even though he tried his best, he still couldn't stretch out his hand

. At that time, De Thich transformed the piece of silk cloth into a bundle of grass. Lo Chi saw this and was extremely embarrassed. The king immediately laughed loudly and said: "Forget it, you don't need to offer silk, if there's anything unjust, just say it quickly."

Lo Chi shed tears and cried as he told the whole story. The king heard it and ordered both Mr. Lo Chi along with his wife and children to come to the palace. The king saw that both people, from voice to appearance, were exactly the same. He immediately ordered them to take off their shirts, bare their arms, and compare their moles to identify them, but they were still identical and indistinguishable. The king immediately ordered the two people to be taken to two separate places, asking each person to write down the most hidden and secret things in their lives. The result is not only the content is the same, but also the handwriting is no different.

At that time, the king lamented: "I am a mortal, and in this matter I am easily confused and cannot distinguish. Now I should go and ask Shakyamuni Tathagata."

After that, he got in the car and went with Mr. Lo Chi to Ky Vien monastery. The Buddha saw him and immediately called out to Lo Chi. De Thich immediately appeared in his true form as a heavenly king. The king saw De Thich, immediately knelt down to worship, then turned to tell Lo Chi to return home. Lo Chi said: "Now when I return home, all my assets have been lost."

Ich Thich said: "You do alms, the assets in the treasury have not changed at all."

Lo Chi got angry and said: "I only believe in Buddha's words, not Ich's words."

Buddha said: "Go back home, what Dei Thich said is not wrong."

Lo Chi returned home, and sure enough, he saw the assets in his possession. The warehouse is still intact with no loss. From then on, he gradually changed his personality, often doing alms to help people, no longer as stingy and stingy as before.1

NOTE 1

The Jade Emperor's punishment caused La Mat to lose all his assets, and was forced into a corner, so embarrassed that he committed suicide. Although De Thich's joke made Lo Chi miserable because he thought all his property was lost, in the end it was returned to him, causing La Mat to repent and transform into a good person. Only then will we know how miraculous the Buddha's Dharma is!

tieu_de: Have pity on lonely people
noi_dung:
PITY FOR THE LONELY

Preach widely

Pitiful! There are so many lonely people in the world, orphans and weak children with no one to rely on. In the past, when my parents were still alive, they were loved and pampered, cared for in every way, and loved like pearls; I also used to be held and cherished, hugged and protected, only worrying about my baby being unusually hot or cold. Who would have thought that their parents would die halfway and soon return to immortality, causing their flesh and blood to separate, surely their parents would not be able to help but be filled with endless pain.

Alas, being human is the most important thing to have

The heart that thinks of itself as loving others is worthy of being called merciful and forgiving. Imagine if your children had to wander adrift, lonely and miserable, and suddenly someone benevolent and generous would help and protect them, how would you appreciate that kindness! Therefore, it can be said that everyone has an impatient heart. When we see others suffering and suffering, we cannot just stand by and watch. If you can often cultivate such thoughts, you are called a person with a kind heart.

At a young age, his parents died early, so of course he became an orphan and lonely. But by extension, those who have no uncles in their relatives, and have few siblings in their families, can also be called lonely. Families with few blessings, old age but still young children, are also called lonely. Like people who, because they are busy with official duties, or jostling around in business, have to drift away from home without relatives, that is also called loneliness. Even people who are virtuous and pure but are slandered and humiliated by others, people who are highly virtuous but are slandered by others, causing everyone to stay away, are also called lonely.

There are many such cases of so-called loneliness, and there are many diverse ways to initiate compassion and help. Below is an article by Emperor Quan, which can help to understand and differentiate more clearly.

Citing the legend

COMMODATION OF FRIENDS AT THE NINE STREETS

Di Quan said: Guan Su Shi was Wei Zhongxiang, a companion. We were in court together and have known each other for a long time. After he died, he had no sons, leaving only five orphaned daughters with no one to rely on. I took full care of the marriage of the three grown children. The remaining two children were entrusted to the house of the Tu Gian mandarin, Cao Chi Luong, and later took me as wives for my two children, Minh and Mau Dung.

Discussion

Orphaned boys who are raised by someone are also common, but orphaned girls who are cared for and cared for are very rare. The Vi family is very lucky to have such a good friend.

About the two sons of Emperor Quan, Minh and Mau Dung, who later in the Western Jin dynasty were reborn as sons of Ta Dong Son. In the Tang Dynasty, there was Prime Minister Truong Cuu Linh, and in the Song Dynasty, there was Prime Minister Truong Te Hien, as well as Sima Quang, both of whom were descendants of the two.

tieu_de: Forgive those who make mistakes
noi_dung:
PEARANCE FOR MISTAKES

Broad explanation

Confucius said: “Correct your own bad points, do not attack and criticize the bad points of others.” He also said: "Be strict with yourself and reduce your criticism of others."

The sages of the past have thousands of admonitions, all advising us to examine our own mistakes. If you know how to examine your own mistakes, you will always be concerned with correcting yourself, and will have no time to blame other people's mistakes.

Sometimes people's mistakes are intentional, sometimes they are just unintentional. Accidental mistakes are easy to forgive, intentional mistakes are difficult to forgive. But religious students who are determined to cultivate tolerance should pay attention to tolerating the intentional mistakes of others. If someone who makes an intentional mistake can still be forgiven, let alone someone who makes an unintentional mistake?

When things are so serious that they cannot be tolerated and we want to tolerate them, it will certainly be very difficult, but we cannot help but try our best. So what methods can be used to initiate forgiveness in these cases?

One ​​is to think about the person committing the mistake because he or she is not wise enough. Most people in the world are ordinary and vulgar people, so why do we want to blame others with the standards of sages? If we cannot forgive those who lack understanding, then it turns out we are the ones lacking wisdom.

Second, think about the shortness of human life. People living in this life, day by day, are like shadows passing through the bars of a door. One day that passes means one day less in life; Just like a death row prisoner on his way to the execution ground, every step is a step closer to death. How can one not have compassion for such a short human life?

Third, thinking about other people's mistakes is the remedy to help us correct our own mistakes. In the past, even if we were at fault, we often did not know it ourselves. Now we see other people's faults, so we can self-reflect and reflect. Therefore, he can be considered my teacher, how dare he judge and blame him?

If you start thinking like the above, you will be able to forgive even the things that are very difficult to forgive. Therefore, when the mind cannot yet be forgiven, the mind is often impatient and irritable; After forgiving someone, your heart will naturally feel peaceful and calm. If you have a hot-tempered mind, you will see plenty of thorns in front of you, even worms and ants are enough to be obstacles on the path. When the mind is at peace, barriers will not be erected, the soul will naturally open up, even those who are at odds with us can move forward on the same path.

Furthermore, if you cannot forgive the person who is at fault, you will have to argue with him or her, causing your self-esteem to be touched, and you will have to find ways to justify it, so you want that person to not make mistakes anymore, but in fact they make more mistakes. On the contrary, if we can forgive another person's mistakes, it will certainly make that person feel ashamed of himself. Even though we don't pray for him not to make mistakes, he will naturally make fewer mistakes.

Therefore, it is said that seeing the faults of others is the gateway to all evil things, but seeing one's own faults is the gateway to all good things.1

NOTE 1

The Mahaparinirvana Sutra teaches that: “Too often be too self-conscious, not to be short-tempered.” (Usually examine your own mistakes, do not talk about other people's shortcomings.) It seems that the meaning is very similar.

Citing stories

RECOMMENDING ENEMIES

Di Quan said: "My father died,1 was originally due to Nam Phong Thanh's slander, everyone in the court knew about it. I still haven't forgotten that lifelong hatred. After Nam Phong Thanh died, his son Nam On Thuc was a talented and virtuous man. The official surnamed Vi often told me: "Nam Phong Thanh's son was eager to learn and never tired of saying anything. all conform to morality and propriety, which is rare among aristocratic children today."

NOTE 1

This recalls the fact that Truong Vo Ky was exiled by King Chu Le and died in Phien Dung land. (Editor's note)

God's will is difficult to know, who would have thought that Nam Phong Thanh would have such a son. At that time Now, even though I have a bitter feud with the Nam family, when I hear about On Thuc's kindness and kindness, I still admire and love him. When I was promoted to the position of Chief Officer, the position of Bao Thi had not yet been replaced, so I immediately recommended On Thuc for that position.

Commentary

King Nghieu killed Mr. Con for failing to manage water, but his son Vu still helped King Nghieu continue the work of water management and did it successfully. Guan Thuc and Sai Thuc were brothers of Chu Cong, both were ordered to be killed by the king,1 but Chu Cong was still the main person helping Chu Thanh Vuong. Emperor Quan, not because of hatred for his father, caused the country to lose talented people, causing virtuous people to be obscured and not used. It can be said that he very skillfully applied the word filial piety.

NOTE 1

In the original version, it was written as “管、蔡為戮” (Quan, Sai vi luc), meaning that both the Governor and Sai Thuc were punished. death sin. But according to some other historical records, when Chu Cong led his army to the east, he only killed Quan Thuc Tien, while Sai Thuc Do was exiled. Sai Thuc Do also had a son, Co Ho, who was a virtuous man, and was later appointed by Chu Cong to succeed him as king of Sai.

When I read the Book of Rites, I saw a sentence that says: "An enemy who kills his father cannot be reconciled." Later, I read the Buddhist scriptures and found a saying: "All hatred cannot be repaid." These two theories may seem completely contradictory, but each has its merits.

Confucians only rely on this present life, so if they take revenge on their father and do not repay it, it means they have forgotten the grace of nurturing them. Therefore, it is considered filial piety to nurture that "unmatched" mind.

The Buddha understood cause and effect in the three lives, past, present and future, and saw that the sentient beings who were our parents in the past are truly countless, and those who are enemies of our parents are also countless. Thus, among the sentient beings who were our parents, they were also each other's enemies, countless in number. There are so many, if each one is irreconcilable, how can one take revenge on all?

What's more, just considering in this life, one more hatred means the parents have to add another resentment, so in order to end the cause of opposition and resentment for the parents, being patient and not taking revenge is considered filial piety.

Consider that when Vu Vuong attacked King Tru, Thai Cong1 carried his halberd and went into battle, Ba Di stood in front of the horse's head, determined to stop him,2 so aren't those two people as opposed to each other as water and fire? But when Mencius mentioned this matter, he said: "Those two old men are both the most respected old men in the world." I also never dared to criticize those two people, who is good and who is bad. All differences or similarities between Confucianism and Buddhism should be considered in that way. If you do so, the more you read Buddhist scriptures, the more you will understand Confucian logic. The Emperor advised people to widely practice following the Three Teachings precisely for that reason.

NOTE 1

Thai Cong, or Thai Cong Vong, or Khuong Thai Cong, that is, Khuong Tu Nha, who led the army to help King Vu attack Tru.

NOTE 2

Ba Di was a sage at that time. He was originally the son of the king of Co Truc, a vassal of the Thuong dynasty, that is, a servant of King Tru. He was offered the throne by his younger brother, Thuc Te, but did not accept it because he did not want to disobey his father's will. He immediately left Co Truc kingdom and later joined Van Vuong. When Van Vuong raised his army to attack Tru, he blocked the horse's head and tried to stop him because he thought it was disloyal.

tieu_de: Widely do good deeds, accumulate virtue, and penetrate the heart of heaven
noi_dung:
DOING WIDELY THINGS
Blessedness, Accumulating Virtue, Understanding
THE HEART OF HEAVEN

Teaching width

In the previous text, from “never tyrannical to people” to here, there are 5 sentences, all talking about the things that the Emperor has done, accumulating virtue, but in fact it is impossible to tell everything, so using the two words “broad do” is to summarize everything.

Originally used the word “yin quality” (陰騭), originally originating from the Thien Hong Pham (洪范) in the book Thuong Thu (尚書). According to the note of Sai Tram (蔡沈) of the Song Dynasty, these are things that have been “put determined” (默定), meaning that in the silent silence, people do not see or know, but there is a silent decision that decides things should be like that. However, understanding it in that sense is not appropriate for the sentence here, but should be understood in the sense of “sound duc” (阴德) is correct.1

NOTE 1

It is according to Mr. An Si's idea that when Vietnamese translate, we often translate it in the sense of "sound virtue", very limited to reuse the word "sound quality" as in the original.

Originally, the word “thuong giang” (蒼穹), meaning “green high”, was used to refer to the high sky. The word “thuong” (蒼) refers to color, the word “frame” (穹) refers to height and breadth.

If we talk about color, like the palace where the gods live, then it fits with the word “love”, because in the sutra it says it has a sparkling color like green lapis lazuli. If we talk about the measurement of height and width, it fits the word “frame”, because the Dao-loi heaven is indeed 84,000 yojanas above our earth.

Citing the story

BECOMING A GOOD OFFICER IN THANH HA

Di Quan said: After I left the evil path, 1 was born in the state of Trieu as the son of Truong Vu, named Truong Huan, and later grew up to be the district commander of Thanh Ha.

NOTE 1

Meaning after the Emperor met the Buddha and heard the Dharma.

Since I became an official, I have always kept a clear mind, been tolerant and benevolent, and could not bear to look down on those below me. Treat subordinates like friends, treat people like family members. If my subordinates make mistakes, I will help them correct them; For lazy people, use words of encouragement and advice; For rude and rough people, patiently teach and bring about repentance; For cunning and cunning people, thoroughly investigate and clarify everything; For those who care about benefits and benefits, teach morality; For those who argue and disparage matters of decency and legality, use sentiment to understand the metaphor; As for the rebels and robbers, we immediately made it clear and forced them to reimburse money

correct; For those who hurt others, we must admit their fault and compensate for the damage; For those who make mistakes for the first time, we can be tolerant, we advise and then forgive; I also forgive those who commit crimes that do not come from a heart that can forgive them; I ran out of words and used all my strength to teach and remind everyone to follow morality and rules. If there is a mistake in the judgment and conviction, and someone criticizes it as condoning bad people, we will listen.

I held the position of district commander for 5 years, the weather was favorable, epidemics did not arise, and every time people made offerings to heaven and earth, they praised me.

Discussion

There were many good officials during the Han Dynasty, but was there anyone who was as merciful, loving, shared the suffering of the people, and felt pain with the people's pain like Emperor Quan? Researching in the bibliography records about mandarins, we only found Truong Vu as an evil and corrupt mandarin, and there was no mention of his son Truong Huan as a virtuous mandarin. So can the bibliographic records be completely trusted?

THE DAI TIEN OF THE SNOW MOUNTAIN

Di Quan said: I entered the reign of King You of Zhou,1 by

NOTE 1

King You of Zhou was the last king of the Western Zhou Dynasty, reigning from 781 BC to 771 BC. U Vuong was tyrannical and immoral, infatuated with Bao Tu, abandoned the crown prince and queen, was led by the queen's father, Marquis Than, to join the army of Tang and Khuyen, Nhung pulled back to attack, had to flee and was killed in Ly Son. Later, his eldest son, Crown Prince Nghi Cuu, became the successor, known as King Chu Binh, starting the Eastern Zhou Dynasty, for the imperial capital to the East.

frankly intervened and was sentenced to death. 1's soul had no place to return, lurking in the palace and mourning for 3 days. The king heard the crying and thought it was a monster, so he ordered mandarin Dinh Thi to follow the crying and shoot arrows. At that time, I left the country of King U and left, with all my heart towards the west.

NOTE 1

At that time, U Vuong was angry with De Quan and frankly intervened, forcing him to drink poisoned wine and die. (Author's note)

I passed through Man Mountain, Nga Mi Mountain, then left Thuc land, flew over many towering mountains, looking to the west there was a mountain peak, both high and wide, estimated to be more than a hundred miles, covered with cold snow, truly not a scene on earth.2 The mountain god Bach Huy told me: "That mountain is called Tuyet Son. In the past, Buddha Tathagata practiced there for 8 years. then attained enlightenment,3 why didn't you stay in that mountain?"

NOTE 2

This mountain is located on the border with Thien Truc (India), near a country called Pham-dien-na. Master Huyen Trang once came to this place. (Author's note)

NOTE 3

Shakyamuni Tathagata once lived on this mountain practicing asceticism for 6 years. If we say Many Treasures Tathagata, then it means the previous Ancient Buddha of this Sage life. How could the mountain god know? Furthermore, the names of Buddhas vary from place to place and are not the same. In the sutra it is said: "One name has countless Buddhas, one Buddha has countless names." Therefore, surely here the mountain god speaks of Many Treasures Tathagata, referring to Shakyamuni Tathagata. (Author's note)

I followed the mountain god's advice and stayed on that mountain. Not long after, the Jade Emperor issued a decree appointing me as Tuyet Son Great Immortal.

Comment

The Emperor is in charge of the academic work of the human world, on par with the gods, thanks to his good deeds that truly reach the heart of heaven, only this one thing is different.

Those who are bestowed by the Jade Emperor must obey the orders of heaven. Even if God can give glory, it can also impose meanness. Only those who practice in this world, or are reborn in the Western Pure Land, or are temporarily reborn in the Four Zen heavens of the Rupa Realm, can be free and independent, without having to follow orders from the Jade Emperor.

tieu_de: If anyone can keep a gentle mind like me
noi_dung:
IF ANYONE CAN KEEP A GOOD MIND
BE GOOD LIKE ME

Teach widely

First you must clearly understand the meaning of the two words “keep your mind”, then explain the meaning “maybe like me”. Furthermore, we first need to understand what "mind" is, then review the meaning of "keeping the mind" and "not keeping the mind". Just like teaching someone to preserve treasure, you must first clearly point out where that treasure is.

main. Confucianists say: "Tao is a great source originating from heaven",1 but that is only a very vague and abstract way of saying it, and is not the principle of the so-called "dao" as passed down from Confucius and Nhan2. Yet, Confucianists intend to blaspheme Buddhism, completely without reason proposing the theory that "Buddha's origin is in the mind, Confucianism's origin is in heaven", not knowing that this is destroying the very profound original "psychology" of Confucianism, voluntarily bringing the most precious treasure of Confucianism to Buddhism, which is extremely unfortunate. There are also ignorant post-graduates who do not understand, but follow that theory and support it. Who knows when will there be a great sage capable of correcting such mistakes?

NOTE 1

This concept was introduced by Dong Trong Thu, a famous Confucianist in the Western Han Dynasty.

NOTE 2

Confucius and Nhan, that is Confucius and Nhan Hoi, are considered the saints of Confucianism.

The education taught by the sages not only helps us to have a free mind, free from all attachments. The mind is free from all attachments, who still comes back to ask for anything else? One mind seeks, one mind escapes, it seems like there are two separate minds. If there are no two separate minds, why make a distinction called seeking and escape? It is here that we must research and ponder diligently, we cannot just consider it superficially.

Confucianism discusses the mind, reaching the theory of “empty clear and unobscured, full of reason, transformed into thousands of things”, which can be considered pure and sophisticated to the extreme. However, that idea originally originated from the explanations in the Avatamsaka and Shurangama sutras of Buddhism. From the time after Confucius and Mencius to before the times of Zhou Dun Di, Trinh Hao, and Trinh Di1, there was no such theory in Confucianism. Chu Hy2 initiated this theory,3 can be considered a contributor to Confucianism.

NOTE 1

Zhu Dun Di, also commonly known as Mr. Liem Khe (濂溪), was a famous Confucian scholar in the Song Dynasty, born in 1017 and died in 1073, who initiated a theory that was later continued to be developed by Trinh Hao (1032-1085) and Trinh Di (1033-1107). All three of them made significant contributions to Confucian doctrine and thought.

NOTE 2

Zhu Xi's full name was Yuan Hoi, courtesy name Hoi Am, born in 1130, died in 1200, was the successor of Zhou Don Di's theory but developed it to a much more complete level.

NOTE 3

Here I want to talk about Zhu Xi's new ideas in the book University of Chapters (大学章句).

At the age of 18, Chu Hy came to study with Luu Binh Son. Luu Binh Son thought that he wanted to follow the academic career path, so he opened his bookcase and saw only one volume of Dai Hue Zen master's book (大慧禪師語錄), nothing else.4 Chu Hy often went with Lu Dong Lai and Truong Nam Hien to visit many virtuous Zen masters everywhere, especially with Zen master Dao Khiem, he had a very secret relationship. set. Mr. Dao Khiem repeatedly gave instructions, often reminding and warning him in his practice.5 Therefore, in Chu Hy's comments and explanations on the books University, Trung Trung,

NOTE 4

This can be seen in Thuong Truc Bien (尚直編) and Kim Thang Bien (金湯編). (Author's note)

NOTE 5

When Zen Master Dao Khiem passed away, Chu Hy composed a funeral poem, which was transcribed in Hoang Giao tap (宏教集). (Author's note)

when discussing the nature of mind, the essential part is very close to Zen thought. In his old age, Chu Hy lived in seclusion in a thatched house with mud walls, often chanting Buddhist scriptures, and composed a collection of poems "Trai Cu Chanting Sutras" (齋居誦經詩). It would be wrong to say that Zhu Xi was completely ignorant of Buddhist scriptures.1

NOTE 1

Once upon a time, Duke Lu discussed with Confucius and said many good things. Confucius praised, Duke Lu said: "That's not what I thought of, I just heard it from you." Confucius replied: "That means the king is following the right way. An upright and upright mind is the way." Considering this, those who love Chu Hy do not need to hide the fact that Chu Hy studied Buddhist scriptures. (Author's note)

EXCUSSION OF THE MIND

THE MIND IS NOT IN

Deluded people often think that the mind is in this body, that's just because they mistakenly perceive the mind that belongs to the six organs inside the body as the mind, or the heart, and think that it is the empty and magical body, without knowing that there is a tangible mind, or heart, that depends on this body, which is constantly born and died, and there is an invisible mind, or consciousness, that does not depend on this body, so there is no birth and death. 2

NOTE 2

Arguments like this seem to have much value only in the original, because Chinese characters use the same character for heart and mind. In Vietnamese, the distinction between the visible heart and the invisible mind is too clear and cannot cause confusion.

The visible mind, or heart, is in the body, and

the invisible mind, or consciousness, is not in the body. If we say that these two minds are just one, then the benevolent and compassionate heart of Nghieu and Thuan and the cruel and tyrannical heart of Kiet and Tru must be as far apart as heaven and earth. Why do we all suffer from mental illness, but in some cases we need to be diagnosed with medication, and in other cases we have to use psychological treatment methods? Therefore, we know that the mind that needs medicine and the mind of good and evil are clearly two different minds.

THE MIND IS NOT OUTSIDE

Some people doubt that the visible mind is not consciousness, so surely our ability to see and know is the mind. But the objects of seeing and knowing are all outside, thus showing that the mind that can see and know is also outside. These people often compare it to closing their eyes and looking inside, unable to see, only able to see the objects facing them, unable to see the shape from inside places such as the eyelashes, bottom of the eyes, or facial skin. Again, like being outside a house, of course you can only see the walls, windows... from the outside, but you can't see the hidden places inside from the outside. Please tell me, that's not true. The ability to know suffering, to know pain, is our mind. Like other people drinking the taste of celandine medicine, we cannot feel a bitter taste in our mouth; Like a mosquito stinging on the skin, we immediately complain of pain, so can we say that the mind is outside?

THE MIND IS NOT IN THE BETWEEN

Some people suspect that the mind is neither inside nor outside, so it must sometimes go inside and sometimes go out, so it must be in the middle. Please tell me, that's not true. If there is in and out, it is not in the middle. If it is determined in the middle, there will be no entry or exit. Furthermore, how can we call it the middle? If we think that the middle is inside the skin, it is still the same as the old theory that the mind is inside. If we think that the middle is outside the skin, it is still the same as the old theory that the mind is outside. Going further to find the middle, but in the wrinkles of the skin are just dirty irritations, can that be our mind?

THE MIND IS NOT BOTH EXISTING AND NOT EXISTING

Or some people say: "If the mind does not exist, then it must not be seen, cannot hear, cannot eat, cannot know taste. But if you can see by looking, hearing by hearing, eating by knowing the taste, that means the mind exists. So, of course, the mind must both exist and not exist?”

Answered: "Those six consciousnesses1 are not the mind. For example, when seeing a beautiful girl, the mind immediately begins to fall in love. That is because the eyes (eye sense) and physical form (physical objects) come into contact with each other, forming awareness (eye consciousness). Hearing about sour apricots, saliva naturally arises

NOTE 1

That is, eye consciousness, ear consciousness, tongue consciousness, body consciousness and consciousness.

in the mouth, it is because the tongue and the sour taste interact with each other that consciousness comes from a very high place, looking down low, the legs naturally tremble, it is because the body and emotions push each other to become consciousness. mile. The ancients said:

The source of birth and death in all lifetimes,
The ignorant person does not know the true mind

This is the meaning

The mind covers nothingness

In the Shurangama Sutra, the Buddha told Ananda: "The emptiness of the ten directions arises in your mind, but it is just like a small cloud in the vast sky."

The Buddha told Ananda seven times to point out the place of the mind; Asking seven times, answering seven times, clearing away all false misconceptions, then gradually revealing the mysterious and clear true mind, causing Ananda to gain temporary enlightenment, which can be said to be an extremely profound and profound display.

Discussion

The word “mind” inherently has a vague and unclear meaning, the word “keep” is even more uncertain. If you are still determined to clearly state the meaning of “keeping your heart”, it will only become more misleading, you should only focus on things from

“never tyrannizing people” as well as “saving people in danger” etc., understanding that that is the place to “keep your heart gentle kind” of the Emperor, just respectfully try to do so.

tieu_de: God must bless you
noi_dung:
BE HEAVEN'S BLESSING
GOOD

Preaching widely

The above sentence says “keep a good mind like me”, that is human; This verse says “heaven bestows blessings”, which is fruit. The word “must be” means certainty, like the person who grows melons must be able to pick melons, the person who plants beans must be able to pick beans, there cannot be the slightest deviation. It is not at all like the theory of those who read the books of saints and sages in vain, saying: "The will of heaven from all eternity can be known; the will of heaven in this dying age cannot be known."

The word “heaven” can refer to visible physical form, that is, the sky; It can also refer to the master of all things. When used to refer to the master of all things, "heaven" means supreme god, or Jade Emperor. Later Confucians avoided using the title "god", so they used the word "ly" (理) instead, but that word really doesn't have enough meaning. Because when people talk about "god", they all mean fear. If we only use the word "reason", no one will fear?

For example, there is a beautiful girl in a closed room. Someone walked into that room and their sexual desires suddenly flared up. Suddenly I heard someone say: "In this room there is a statue of the Jade Emperor. That girl came here to offer incense." At that time, even an extremely evil person would still have to feel fear, not necessarily right in front of the Jade Emperor's statue and dare to let loose and act rashly. But if instead you hear someone say: "If you do such arrogant things, it is completely not according to reason. Instead, it goes against reason, that is, you offend the very name of the holy religion, you cannot be called a gentleman." Let's ask if that person, while his sexual desire is raging strongly, can he suddenly extinguish it after hearing those words?

So we know that using the word "heaven" to refer to the Jade Emperor's ability to advise and educate students is truly a merit to Confucianism. If we only use the word "reason", it opens the door to freedom and freedom from fear for people in the world, so we cannot use it to teach and teach. That's why the ancients said: "Everyone knows how to fear and obey the principles, that is the clue to the world being in peace. Everyone does not know how to be afraid, that is the clue that causes the world to be in great chaos."

What's more, in this world, all things have no place outside the principles of logic. If we say "heaven" is reason,1 then "nature" is also reason; Confucianists called the destiny of heaven

NOTE 1

The concept of "reason" is one of the developments in philosophical content in Confucianism through the efforts of Confucian scholars from Trinh Hao, Trinh Di and later to absorb and perfect it. Trinh Hao advocates: "Heaven is reason", thereby considering reason as the source and essence of the universe, so it is heaven. Appendix 2 questions and answers

1. WHY ARE THERE SO MANY SCENES OF HEAVEN?

Question: Speaking of heaven, that is the name of the supreme being, no one can equal it to be called heaven, how come there are so many different names and shapes?

Answer: Humans are also considered spiritual beings in all things, can they only be called people without distinguishing between the wise and the foolish, the noble and the lowly? The Sutras teach that: "If you keep the Five Precepts, you will be born in the human world; if you practice the Ten Good Karmas, you will be born in the heavenly world." However, in following the Five Precepts and the Ten Good Karmas, there are different levels, more or less, deep and shallow. Therefore, in the human world, each person's blessings are not the same. The gods in the heavenly realms are the same, each of them's blessings are not the same.

2. THE DIVISION OF THE SAINTS IN HEAVENLY SCENES

Question: Of the 28 heavenly realms mentioned above, which heavenly realm is mortal and which heavenly realm is holy?

Answer: There are 2 heavens that belong to mortals, 5 heavens that belong to saints. The remaining 21 heavens are all places where mortals and saints reside.

The two heavens that belong to mortals are the Great Brahma Heaven of the First Zen Heaven and the Non-Perception Heaven of the Four Zen Heavens.

In addition to the 7 heavenly realms mentioned above, the remaining 21 heavenly realms are all places where there are two mortals and saints. It can be inferred that they are all due to receiving blessings from practicing good karma in the two realms of heaven and human.

When Dang Doanh heard what happened, he felt compassion and said to the man: "Because you are sick, you can't plow the field, it's not your fault. Even though I'm poor, I can still live on my own, how can I let you and your father separate? Quickly bring money to redeem my child." But the owner who bought the child did not agree to redeem it. Dang Doanh immediately said: "I'm just a poor scholar, but I can still afford not to rent fields; that family is rich and must know about cultivating virtue, I will go there to convince you." Having said that, he went with the tenant to the house where the owner had bought the child. They immediately helped him to redeem him, and father and son were reunited.

Oh, what a pity for farmers, all year round

they work hard and never have time to relax; The whole family is suffering together, no one is safe; Both shoulders carry the burden of carrying manure from the house to the field, and the two shoulders carry the burden of carrying the load of rice from the field to the house; In the year of drought, I used buckets of water to save rice, but on sick days I still had to work hard to plow; stooped over, weathered by sun and rain, heartbroken and hungry; Once the rice is ripe and harvested, all taxes and measuring bowls will be clean; The four-walled house is primitive, the poverty is constant, and how can we rely on eight mouths to feed? If a kind-hearted person saw this scene, how could he not feel compassion?

Once upon a time, there was Chu Canh Duong. Every time he heard that a tenant farmer had a funeral, he would shed tears and immediately give money to help. The tenants who rented the fields were grateful for his virtue and never missed or fell short of their payments. The small-minded landowners compared every detail with the tenants, thinking that they were getting a lot of profit, little did they know that in that obscure place, there was an extremely sophisticated and accurate calculation of cause and effect. Could it be that this did not end all their blessings? Explaining widely

Tong Giao's story, many people believe is nothing more than a small good deed but the retribution is so great that it gives rise to doubt. However, thinking like that is not really knowing that, that is just stating the immediate task, when we see saving the ants, we say saving the ants, when we see the poinsettia beans, we say we save the ants. If we discuss this thoroughly, Tong Giao's actions saved the lives of at least tens of thousands of lives, so in the next life there must be tens of thousands of lives who thank him for saving their lives and try to repay him. So how can the mere act of passing the poinsettia be worthy of reaping the blessings

of that act? What's more, dong poinsettia is just a bit of an empty name on the outside; Three inches of breath has just passed, life is gone, is there still a poinsettia left? Therefore, if anyone says that such retribution is too great, he is truly wrong.

Placing bamboo branches to pray for help from the ants is a flood rescue. But the lives of ants do not just die due to floods, so saving ants is not limited to placing bamboo branches as bridges. For example, if there is a maid in your house who wants to use boiling water and hot fire to destroy an ant nest, the way to save the ants' lives at that time is to use morality to explain to the listener, and also use your power to prevent them from doing it.

Dogs and cats in the house can also kill ants, when food such as meat, fish... is scattered on the ground, causing sniffing ants to gather and cling to it, which is then eaten by dogs and cats mixed with that food. Therefore, to save ants from being killed, after each meal, you should clean up food scattered on the ground and bury it so it does not become bait for ants.

Burning votive papers, paper... things can also kill ants, mainly because burning in the early morning cannot be seen clearly. To save ants from dying in this way, you should sweep the ground clean before burning, spread a lot of cool ash first as a base and then burn on top of that ash base.

Drinking tea can kill ants, mostly by pouring excess water on the ground. To save ants from dying because of this method, you should use sinks or pots to store excess water without pouring it on the ground.

Near the kitchen there are often many ant nests, because they smell the food and gather and make a nest. To save ants from dying in this way, when cooking, you should use limestone to cover the surrounding ground...

Just a few cases, from there we can extrapolate that protecting the lives of all insects, ants... also requires such compassion.

He immediately used a rope tied to the reed tree to pull it along with the boat, and finally brought the ant to shore.

That night, Dong Chieu Chi dreamed that a man dressed in black came to him to thank him, saying: "I am the king of ants. Because of my carelessness, I fell into the river. Today I need your help. In the future, when you are in danger, please come and let me know."

A turtle, when alive, does not know its own life or death. Yet, after death, the skin and flesh are damaged, leaving only the turtle's shell, which has the ability to predict good and bad events for people in the world. Explanation

Dragons have four deadly poisons. Sometimes people die from being bitten; Sometimes you die from touching it; Sometimes you die from seeing it; Or sometimes you die from hearing their sounds. Snakes also have four similar poisonous qualities. The snake that Thuc Ngao saw must have been the type that could make people die when they saw it.

According to the words of the people of So, to this day that two-headed snake still exists. This snake has a yellow body, about a meter long, and can crawl forward or backward when moving, very similar to an earthworm. At first glance, it doesn't seem harmful, certainly

now it is a different species, because all species change over time. For example, all animals in ancient times could speak human language, but today no species can speak. In the mind that contains evil things, most of them will turn into snakes, centipedes, scorpions... People with a compassionate and attentive mind cannot be harmed by all kinds of poison. If that's not the case, then when there is something harmful outside, we also use the harmfulness to respond, that is, a snake on the outside plus a snake in the mind. I did not have the ability to tame poisonous snakes, so how could I let myself be assimilated by poisonous snakes and become as toxic as snakes?

Poisonous snakes are animals that harm people, so Thuc Ngao buried the snake to avoid others from seeing it. If we extrapolate accordingly, everything that harms others can be considered poisonous snakes. When we can do things to eliminate destruction and eliminate violence, it means burying the poisonous snakes that walk on two legs. Trying to correct mistakes made in the past, practicing towards good deeds in the future, is burying the poisonous snake in your mind.

From the sentence "Vu Cong tried the case" until this sentence in the main text, Emperor Quan Su raised cases of doing good deeds to receive blessings to teach people. If one person does good deeds and receives blessings, everyone who does good deeds will also receive blessings. Just like tasting a fruit

The paragraph from here onwards down to state what should be done to encourage, urge, and generalize the key points to nurture good roots in the mind. Expressions such as “often constantly doing helping people” do not need any further explanation, but saying “silently doing all kinds of merit” is also so clear. When doing things to help others, it is important to do it regularly without interruption; To silently create merit, it is important to try to do everything, not to underestimate or omit, even if it is just a small thing. If we speak according to worldly dharma, it is indeed very difficult to do so. But if you know how to apply Buddhism thoroughly, it is not difficult at all. If you see a good deed that you can do with your own strength, immediately

Enthusiastically jump in and try to do it right away. If you see a good deed that your strength cannot bear, then make a great vow, and wait until your next life when you have enough ability to do it.

Explanation on vows

Worldly blessings

If you are in a place of government administration, may all good policies reach people across the country; If you live in the countryside, may everyone enjoy eternal peace. As for your father-child relationship, may it be a good father and a good child; As for your brotherhood, I pray that you will always maintain cordiality and politeness. When I have food to eat, I pray that the hungry people in the world will be well-fed. When I myself have clothes, may those who are suffering from rags and cold be warm with enough blankets and clothes. Passing through the market place, may all homes be filled with plenty; Walk through the dike roads and fields, praying that every year there will be good rain and wind. Seeing people crossing rivers and seas, pray that they will not encounter strong winds and waves; Seeing people going into dangerous mountains and forests, I pray that they will not be harmed by snakes, centipedes, or tigers. Seeing the poor and suffering, pray for them to be rich and wealthy; I hear that people are sick and suffering, and I pray that they will be strong and peaceful. Seeing others achieve achievements is like achieving yourself; Seeing someone fail is also considered a failure yourself.If you can

in every thought, always remember to think of such wishes, not letting them go away, then expanding your love for people in the four seas like brothers, harmonizing all things with yourself as one is not difficult?

Comment

These are just worldly blessings. Why is that? Because although we know how to think about good deeds in this life, we do not know that there are many other lives; I only worry that in this life I won't be able to help others, but I don't know that as long as I keep my wish, in future lives it will definitely come true. Furthermore, the above vows are only limited to the human realm, not extending to the heavens, hell, hungry ghosts, or animals. Such wishes, even if all are fulfilled as desired, and sentient beings in the six realms will benefit thanks to the grace of virtue, but they will only create retributions to enjoy within the two realms of heaven and human, and cannot help people uproot the cycle of birth and death. That is why people with great wisdom cannot help but develop a deep and profound wish to be born into this world.

The four vows of the world are wide and deep

All sentient beings are boundless, vowing to save everyone.
Endless afflictions, vow to end them all.
Immeasurable Dharma, vow to practice.
Buddhism is unsurpassed, the vow is fulfilled.

Comment

These are the four broad and profound aspirations of Bodhisattvas, each sentence contains countless profound and mysterious meanings. Anyone who is able to understand these four sentences, so that while walking, standing, lying down, and sitting, they never stop, then right there is Bodhi. In the sutras it is taught that: "Practicing without generating the Bodhi mind is like plowing a field without bringing water into it. Even if you try hard to generate good wishes in the world, going through a life like the sands of the Ganges River, is not as good as someone who can only temporarily generate the Bodhi mind."

Evidence

THREE PEOPLE GROWING TOGETHER PRAYER1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from Ajatasatru Sutra - 阿闍世經. (Author's note)

In the past, countless eons ago, there was a Buddha named Tathagata Tathagata. At that time, a wealthy noble family had three young children. One day, all three children brought three pearls to make offerings to Buddha. One child said: "I want to be like the monk standing at the right side of the Buddha in the future." Another child said: "I want to be like the monk standing on the left side of the Buddha in the future." The third child said: "In the future I want to be like the Buddha sitting in the midst of the assembly."

Buddha Shakyamuni told this story and taught: "The child vows to become a Buddha, which is me today. The child wants to be like the monk standing to the left of the Buddha, now Sariputta. The child wants to be like the monk standing to the right of the Buddha, now Maudgalyayana."

SIGNS WITH ANCIENT BUDDHA1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Nirvana Sutra - 涅槃經. (Author's note)

The World-Honored One of ancient times, countless eons ago as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, heard that the Buddha at that time, named Shakyamuni Van Phat, was preaching the Nirvana Sutra, and immediately sold his body to have money to buy incense and flowers to offer to the Buddha. Hearing a verse in the Nirvana Sutra, I made a vow: "I vow that in my future life I will become a Buddha, with the same name as this Buddha." Because of such a vow, today the World-Honored One has the title Sakyamuni Buddha.

DEVELOP THE VOW TO SAVE PEOPLE FIRST2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book Diamond Sutra - 金剛經解. (Author's note)

In countless lifetimes ago, the World-Honored One was once born as a patient immortal. One day, the fairy was sitting deep in the mountain, when suddenly the king came there hunting, chasing an animal that ran past the fairy. The king saw him sitting there and immediately asked which direction the animal ran. The fairy thought: "If you tell the truth, you will kill the animal. If you don't tell the truth, you will commit a lie." He was silent like that for a long time without answering. The king got angry and cut off one of his arms. Asked again, still pensive without answering, the king cut off his remaining arm. At that moment, the immortal immediately made a vow: "This person is cruel. In the future, when I become Buddha, I vow to first save him and not let people imitate him in doing evil deeds." Indeed, when Śākyamuni Buddha had just attained enlightenment, he first preached the Dharma for salvation to Kieu Tran Nhu, the former king.

FORTY EIGHT GREAT Vows1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Maha Amitabha Sutra - 大阿彌陀經. (Author's note)

Amitābha Buddha countless eons ago had a previous incarnation as a monk Phap Tang, who made 48 great vows, including the vow: "When I become a Buddha, may that land be pure, precious, beautiful and dignified. Sentient beings in the ten directions, if anyone wishes to be born in my land, just recite my name, then at the time of death I will manifest the body of a Buddha or Bodhisattva to come and save me." May that person be reincarnated in my land, born from the lotus flower, and attain a state of no longer regressing."

Therefore, today anyone who can single-mindedly recite Amitābha Buddha will be reborn in his Pure Land.

Thanks to vows, it is easy to transform degrees2

NOTE 2

Excerpted from the book of Distinctive Laws - 經律異相. (Author's note)

During the Buddha's time, there was a village full of people who indulged in wrong views and did not believe in the Buddha's teachings. The Buddha told Maudgalyayana to come and teach, and the whole village immediately listened to his teachings and changed their minds toward Buddhism.

Therefore, the Buddha taught: "The people of that village have a predestined relationship with Maudgalyayana. Once upon a time Maudgalyayana was a woodcutter who went up the mountain to collect firewood. One day, he encountered a beehive, and a whole flock of bees flew out, eager to sting him. The woodcutter immediately taught: 'All flying creatures already have Buddha nature, so don't do harmful things. The day after I'm born When he attains enlightenment, he will save all of you.' When the bees heard that word, they all flew away without harming the woodcutter. The villagers today are the same as the bees of the past. Because of Maudgalyayana's vow to save them, now he only needed to come and teach them once and immediately listen."

HERE YOU HAVE JUST DEVELOPED YOUR MIND AND HAVE GONE ABOVE THE TWO YANA1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Treatise on Wisdom - 智度論. (Author's note)

There was an Arhat who had attained the Six Divine Powers. One day he led a novice monk carrying his bag containing his robe and bowl. At that time, the novice monk had a wish in his heart: "I must diligently practice diligently to seek Buddhahood." The Arhat immediately turned back to take the bag containing the robe and bowl to carry it himself, and told the novice monk to go forward.

Just a moment later, the novice monk had the idea: "Praying for Buddhahood is very far away and difficult to achieve. It's better for me to pray for Sravakas, and I will soon be liberated." The Arhat then immediately placed the bag containing his robe and bowl on the novice monk's shoulder, telling him to go to the back.

The Arahant replied: "I am not mistaken, just because before you had the intention to seek Buddhahood, that is, to be in the Bodhisattva position, your position must be higher than mine, so I had to follow behind and carry my bag myself, not daring to let you carry it. Right after that, you again developed a desire for the fruit of a Sravaka, no longer had the thought of saving sentient beings, your status was lower than mine, of course you had to follow behind to carry my bag."

The novice monk heard his teacher say what he meant, and was terrified. From then on, his mind was steadfast and he wholeheartedly and diligently sought Buddhahood.

Comment

The Upasaka Sutra (優婆塞戒經) teaches that: “When a person develops the Bodhi mind,1 all the gods are extremely surprised and happy, thinking that now there is a teacher in the two heavens, people.”2

Develop the mind of Bodhi, that is, develop the mind to seek Buddhahood to save all sentient beings.

Just saying that you have just made a wish, of course it can be understood as having never experienced the practice of attaining enlightenment, thus surpassing Arhatship.3 That is because you have made a wish, one day it will surely be fulfilled. tieu_de: Benefiting people and animals
noi_dung:
BENEFITS PEOPLE AND BENEFITS ANIMALS

Expounding

Speaking of “benefiting animals”, that is enough merit to benefit all things; say "benefit people", that is enough merit to benefit everyone. Being able to benefit all people and all things means living a life that is not in vain.

The word "benefit" has extremely bad connotations and also has extremely good connotations, but not both at the same time. If people seek benefits for themselves, that is their own will, and it is definitely not good. If someone seeks benefits to help many people, that is fair-minded, it must be very good.

Citing the story

THE BEER BREAKER AND THE BEER CARVER1

NOTE 1

Excerpt from the book Divine Induction - 感應篇註(Author's note)

During the Tang Dynasty, there was a famous physician, Ton Tu Mac, who learned 30 good medicinal recipes from Dragon Palace. They used them and were always effective. He recorded them into the book Thien Kim Phuong (千金方), and carved them into stone stele to pass on to future generations.

Someone printed out many copies of this book and immediately destroyed the stone stele in the hope of selling the book for profit. Then he was struck by lightning and died.

There was another person who followed the book and engraved it on the stone stele. Then he dreamed that Ton Tu Mac said: "You originally had no children, but now thanks to the merit of engraving the book Thien Kim Phuong on the stone stele, you will certainly have a noble son."

Afterwards, that person indeed gave birth to a precious child.

Comment

The person who destroyed the stone stele only knew to seek his own benefit, while the person who re-carved the stone stele only thought of benefiting all people. But in the end, those who seek their own benefit will never benefit, but those who benefit all people will always benefit.

CANCEL BAD POLICY1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Hoang Minh Thong Giam -皇明通鑒. (Author's note)

During the Xuande era of the Ming Dynasty,2 the court often sent eunuchs to send people to the West to search for treasures, spending countless amounts of money and causing countless people to die on the way. During the reign of King Anh Tong in the year Thien Thuan,3 someone reported to the king to repeat. The Emperor immediately ordered the Minister of Military Affairs, Hang Trung, to find the book recording that job to carry out. At that time, Liu Dai Ha, who was holding the position of Lang Trung, immediately sneaked into the library first and hid the books. The mandarins who came later could not find anything, and in the end the matter had to be abolished. Later, Minister Xiang Zhong brought up the loss of books and reprimanded his subordinates. Liu Dai Xia immediately laughed and said: "That is a bad policy. For example,
