If that book is still there, it should be destroyed to eliminate it completely, let alone asking what is the point of asking whether the book is still or lost?

Hang Trung was frightened when he heard it, apologized and said: "Your virtue is truly touching to the heavens. My official position should belong to you."

Indeed, Liu Dai Ha later became the official Tai Bao Dai Sima, and his descendants for many generations were honored and rich.

Commentary

According to Liu Dai Ha's actions, if fully expanded, worldly books are harmful to people. should all be destroyed, the most dangerous of which are pornographic novels and books that slander Buddhism.

NORMAL STABILITY OF FOOD PRICES1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Khuyen chung luc - 勸懲錄 (Note by editor fake)

When Truong Quai Nhai was a governor in Chengdu, one day he dreamed that Tu Phu Chan Quan invited him to meet. Not long after arriving, I heard an announcement: "Hoang Kiem Te is coming from the west gate." Immediately seeing a Taoist with a turban on his head entering, Tu Phu Chan Quan greeted him with the utmost respect.

The next morning, Truong Quai Nhai sent someone to the west gate of the citadel. There was indeed a Taoist named

Hoang Kiem Te, who immediately invited him in to meet him. It turned out to be exactly the same as the person he had met in his dream. Truong Qua Nhai immediately asked the Taoist what kind of good deeds he usually did in ordinary life. The Taoist replied: "I really can't do much. Every year, when the rice is ripe, I spend 300 francs to buy rice to store. Next year, when the rice season is not yet ripe, most of the poor people will have a hard time making enough to eat, so I immediately sell that rice at the same price. So I won't lose anything, but the poor people will be helped through the emergency. That's all I can do."

Truong Quai Nhai, after hearing this, was extremely impressed and praised, ordered someone to invite the Taoist to sit on a high throne and then respectfully perform the ceremony himself.

Comment

Keeping food prices stable like that can be done anywhere. As long as people in one place enjoy favors, all four directions should follow suit.

tieu_de: Doing good deeds accumulates merit
noi_dung:
DOING GOOD AND ACQUIRING Blessings

Extensive preaching

What secular people accumulate, there are things that others can plunder, but that we ourselves cannot take with us when we die. There are things that other people cannot take away, but we ourselves cannot take them with us when we die. There are things that we can take with us when we die that others cannot take away.

Gold, silver, jewels, houses, fields, gardens... those are things that others can rob, but we cannot take with us when we die. Scholarly knowledge, outstanding talent, these are things that others cannot take away, but we cannot take them with us when we die.

As for the things that we can take with us when we die but that others cannot rob, it is nothing more than the good deeds we have done and the merits we have created. Doing good to the highest level can help all seven generations of ancestors be promoted to heaven, and all the gods will support them; Accumulating blessings to the highest level can make floods and fires harmless.

Doing good deeds is the foundation of cultivating merit, and merit is the inspiration from doing good deeds. If you only cultivate blessings without cultivating wisdom, every time you enjoy blessings, you will create more bad karma. If you only cultivate wisdom without cultivating blessings, you are afraid that in the next life your blessings will be thin and your life will have to endure many hardships and deprivations.

Once upon a time, during the time of Buddha Kasyapa, there were two brothers who both became monks. The older brother maintained the precepts and meditated, wholeheartedly seeking the Dharma, but did not

cultivate almsgiving. The younger brother diligently cultivates blessings but often violates the precepts. Later, when Śākyamuni Buddha became Buddha, his brother attained Arahantship, but because he had never cultivated merit, he was often hungry and could not eat enough. The younger brother often broke the precepts so he had to be born as an elephant. However, because he often cultivated blessings in his previous life, even though he was born as an animal, he was loved by the king. He often had his body filled with precious pearl bracelets, and gave food to hundreds of households, and food was often abundant. Therefore it is said: "Cultivating blessings without cultivating wisdom, the elephant's body carries a string of pearls. Cultivating wisdom without cultivating blessings, Arhats are often hungry."

Only the Buddha is honored as the Two Perfect One, because both his blessings and wisdom are complete.

Citing the story

CREATING MANY HUMAN BEINGS1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Y Hanh Luc - 懿行錄. (Author's note)

During the Ming Dynasty, in Hoa Dinh district, there was a man named Co Chanh Tam, whose given name was Trong Tu. His father, Co Trung Lap, was a Councilor in Guangxi.

Chanh Tam likes to do good deeds, often donating up to 104,700 taels of silver, buying up to 40,800 acres of land, using it to help others, called meaning dien. Those fields are scattered in the two districts of Hoa Dinh and Thanh Pho. The harvested income is all used to provide tax revenues for farmers in difficult times, helping them not to fall into poverty.

One ​​year, near the end of the year, a patrolling mandarin came to Tung Giang district and issued a strict order prohibiting people on New Year's Eve from lighting fires or lighting fireworks... Some people in the street violated the ban, the mandarin sent someone to arrest them, and mistakenly arrested Co Chanh Tam and put him in prison. On that occasion, he met prisoners who were ragged and cold, and immediately provided them with clothes; When we meet hungry people, we immediately give them food; Those who commit crimes that can be redeemed with money immediately ask to pay money on their behalf; leaving the rescued prisoners in the prison almost empty. Chanh Tam also provided money to renovate the prison. He often did favors for many people even though he knew they had no ability to repay him.

After his death, the local mandarins reported those good deeds to the court, and the emperor gave him all praise, allowing him to be worshiped with the local virtuous ancestors.

Discussion

During the Song Dynasty, Pham Trong Yem bought a field to use the harvested fruits to help people in the Pham family, called Nghia Dien, leaving an eternal reputation. But the Pham family's righteous field only helps people with the same Pham family name, not people with different family names; That field was only about a hundred acres, not more than forty thousand. Co Chanh Tam's beautiful work, far surpassing his predecessors, is truly extraordinary. According to the blessings of that deed, now he is definitely reborn in the Six Desires heaven, flying freely in the air, enjoying endless peace.

ONE LONELY TAKES ON CHARGE

During the Ming Dynasty, in Huzhou, Zhejiang province, there was a man named Tu Nhu Huy, a wealthy family, who liked to give alms to help people. At that time, there was a temple in Hangzhou that organized a precept ceremony, at great expense, officials from both the Bo Chanh and An Sat companies gathered together, calling on the local rich people to contribute.

Tu Nhu Huy voluntarily asked to be left alone to take care of everything. The Governor, Duong Ke Tong, asked why he did so. Tu Nhu Huy replied: "Even if a person has accumulated a fortune, if he has a spoiled child, it will all end up in someone else's hands. Why should he use it for this outstandingly good cause, in the next life he will forever enjoy blessings? What's more, money is a gathering point for hatred. If my child doesn't have money, he won't have to bear the hatred, he will definitely be loved by others."

Nhu Huy offered a thousand pieces of silver. The officials of both the Bo Chanh and San Sat companies all praised his wisdom and generosity, especially setting up an honorary seat in the back hall to invite him. All the officials of his colleagues gathered together to entertain him, and respectfully presented him with a silk curtain and sent him off to his home. Everyone who hears about this is in awe and admiration. 1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Dai Bao Tich Sutra (大寶積經), part of the Dai Chanh Tan Tu Canon, volume 11, sutra number 310, a total of 120 volumes, translated by Bodhisattva in the Tang Dynasty. This excerpt starts from line 16 of page 475, sheet c of volume 82.

Tu Nhu Huy did so to create lasting treasure.

GIVING alms and offerings without tiring

At the end of the Ming Dynasty, in the Zhejiang region, there was a person with the surname Su who liked to do good deeds, often gave alms to help people, and was very happy to organize monks to make offerings. At that time, there was a monk whose name was Dai Thanh. He often came down from the mountain to transform and bring it back to the temple to make offerings to the monks. On the way back to the temple, we passed by the Su family. One day, when we saw the monk returning with rice not filling his bowl, Su Quan immediately went into the house to get more rice to fill it up. It's been like this for many years, and I've never felt discouraged or tired.

One ​​day, Su Quan's wife was about to give birth when she suddenly saw Venerable Dai Thanh coming to the house and went straight to her room. Everyone who saw it was horrified. They quickly chased after him but couldn't find anything. After that, the lady gave birth to a baby boy. The military quickly sent people to the temple to inquire about monk Dai Thanh, only to learn that on the same day

he passed away. That military historian immediately named his son Su Dai Thanh.

The baby is extremely intelligent, from the moment he was in the womb, he made the mother eat only light vegetarian foods. As he matured, his literature became more and more extraordinary. In the year of At Mui, the reign of Thuan Tri1, he passed the Poinsettia exam.

NOTE 1

That is the year 1655. The Shunzhi era of the Qing Dynasty started from 1644 to 1661.

Discussion

Only knowing how to do good deeds without believing in Buddha's teachings, this way of cultivating blessings, the wise person sees as a clue to the unjust karma of the third life. Why is that? Because of that good deed, in the two lifetimes of enjoying the blessings, it is inevitable that many sins will be created, and in the third life, one must receive the karmic retribution of suffering. The historical king was originally a person of Buddhism, so even though he enjoyed wealth and glory, he still did not become infatuated and ignorant because of that.

tieu_de: Integrity acts on behalf of heaven and teaches people
noi_dung:
INTEGRITY REPLACES HEAVEN ACTION, TEACHING PEOPLE

Preaching widely

To say “righteousness” means there is nothing evil or wrong; Saying "straight" means there is nothing to hide or avoid. Therefore, integrity is the rule of heaven.

Ordinary people can act righteously, that is, following the will of heaven to teach others, not necessarily someone sitting on a high throne looking down on all people? If you want to change heaven and practice religion, you don't need to be the ruler or have a lot of power, because even if you want to, you can't have it. Acting on behalf of heaven and teaching people is to obey heaven and earth to transform all things, to participate with heaven and earth to become one of the three elements of the universe: heaven, earth, humanity. To do so, we must first focus our efforts on the word "practice". In that word "practice", of course all business activities, planning, and planning are included, which can be arranged and applied appropriately depending on the time. Calmly and carefully consider the meaning of the next sentence below: “extend kindness, save the people for the country”, it is truly acting on behalf of heaven to teach people, but it seems like it only wants to speak specifically to the officials and generals holding positions of power.

Those who live intelligently and uprightly will certainly become gods after death, that argument is certain for the world. In layman's terms, that is called transcendence, but if you use clear understanding to contemplate, that is falling. That's because worldly people only know the second life but don't know the third life after that. Once you are a god, you must enjoy offerings, most of which are offered by people who kill and harm animals. Having enjoyed these things, in the next life one cannot avoid falling into hell and animal realms, which is just a matter of happening in the blink of an eye

only. Therefore, while teaching people on behalf of heaven, we must always be alert to the potential danger of being reborn into the divine realm, must urgently seek rebirth in the Pure Land, and clearly establish a direction for our lives. We must regularly generate broad and deep vows, and based on that, solidify the foundation of the Bodhi mind. Only then can we avoid the danger of falling into evil realms.

Every day, I wish for others to do many good deeds and accumulate positive virtue, which is pleasing to God. Having a worried heart, fearing that others will fall into error and create bad karma, is also following the will of heaven. Foolish people only see the deep blue space up there and think it is heaven. They do not know that there are actually gods like the Four Kings and the Dao-Loi Thien, who every day observe the good and evil deeds of the worldly people. Is there an easy time for this act of acting on behalf of heaven and teaching people?

Citing the story

EXAMINING GOOD AND EVIL1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the Abhidhamma Discourse -立世阿毗曇論. The Emperors and Heavenly Kings went up together to the Thien Dharma Hall, with the gods accompanying them

respectfully surrounding them. After entering Thien Dharma Hall, De Thich sat on the lion's throne, on both left and right sides, each with 16 heavenly kings sitting together. In addition, all the gods also sat down according to their positions. The four heavenly kings sit at the four doors.

At that time, the four heavenly kings brought the good and evil deeds of the worldly people and presented them to Indra. If he heard that there were many people in the world who kept the Five Precepts, 1 Eight Precepts,2 or treated their parents, monks, and senior monks with respect, practiced almsgiving, and cultivated blessings, Indra would be very happy, knowing that in the future there will be many people born in the heavenly realms, but few people born in the asura realm.3 If that is not the case,

Therefore, when seeing more sentient beings doing good deeds and being born in the heavenly realm than in the asura realm, De Thich was happy.

tieu_de: Expand your kindness, for the country to save its people
noi_dung:
EXPANSION OF MERCY,
FOR THE COUNTRY TO SAVE THE PEOPLE

Preach widely

The people are the root of the country. Only if the roots are strong will the country be at peace, so if you want to help the people, you must have patriotism; Because we love our country, we must be loyal to Minh Quan. The previous sentence is a general statement to educate people, but this sentence is a special warning to those who hold power.

People respectfully call government officials Elders, what does that mean? That is to use the form of address to remind people who are officials to wake up and treat the people like parents treat their children.

Parents are worried about their sick children. Collecting heavy taxes is a disease of the people. Thieves and thugs are becoming more and more rampant, it is a disease of the people. Untimely rain and sunshine, crop failures, are the diseases of the people. The rich are dishonest and brutally exploit, the crooked officials abuse their power to harm the people, these are the people's diseases.

When people suffer from an illness, officials must immediately have a method to help and cure the illness. We must wholeheartedly worry and find every way to cure the people's diseases. Only then will the top not disappoint the leader of the country, the bottom will not disappoint the people, and we ourselves will not be in vain in studying and cultivating knowledge. With that being said, "expanding kindness" is not difficult at all?

Citing stories

FINDING WAY TO SAVE PEOPLE1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book Hoang Minh Thong Ky -皇明通紀. (Author's note)

During the reign of King Tuyen Tong of the Ming Dynasty,2 the patrol officer of Nam Truc was Chu Tham (later given the posthumous title Van Tuong) who loved the people like his own children, and managed public spending strictly and transparently like no one else. When he first took office, he immediately examined the hardships and sufferings of the people, and was extremely concerned and worried about the taxes in the two regions of Suzhou and Tung Giang being too heavy. One year there was a good harvest and the people's harvest was very large. He immediately used his own funds to buy rice and store it in the warehouse in case it was needed for relief purposes. In the 8th year of Tuyen Duc's reign,3 presented a petition in the winter asking for a method to establish rice warehouses to help farmers. The Emperor had the order approved, so he and the prefects of To Chau, Huong Chung, the governor of Tung Giang, Trieu Du, and the governor of Chang Chau, Mac Ngu, discussed and made efforts to implement it. The Suzhou region purchased 300,000 rice jellies, along with Tung Giang and Changzhou also brought in a lot, all divided and stored in food warehouses.

NOTE 2

That is during the period from 1425 to 1435.

NOTE 3

That was the year 1433.

The following year, Jiangnan region suffered from drought, the number of hungry people in Suzhou and Songjiang reached more than 3 million people, rice for relief was distributed but it was not enough. On that occasion, Chu Tham tried to think of ways to store more food. Looking back to the past, when the government collected food during the ripe rice season, they all assigned it to the chiefs in the villages. Most of them only collected food from ordinary people, not from dignitaries in the village. Therefore, people have to pay more, causing every year many people who cannot afford to pay taxes have to flee to live elsewhere.

Chu Tham immediately changed his method, right in the prefectures everywhere, he set up food collection points, choosing people to be in charge from collecting food to transporting it to the warehouse. Farmers directly bring rice to hand over at collection points, no longer going through village chiefs, thereby reducing costs by up to a third compared to before.

In addition, reviewing the previous regulations, every year all three governments must transport 1,000,000 food jelly to the warehouse in Nanjing, then use it for expenses as well as monthly salaries for soldiers and officials in Beijing. tieu_de: Treat people with loyalty
noi_dung:
IN TREATMENT WITH PEOPLE, YOU MUST KEEP LOYALTY
Loyalty

Preaching widely

The word “loyalty” comes from the person's heart, not by looking at the respectful appearance on the outside. know outside. Therefore, helping people limit disasters and prevent tribulations is loyalty. Helping others display goodness and prohibit evil and wrongdoing is also loyalty. Because people go back and forth, that is middle. Giving your best to serve the leader of the country is also loyalty.

It's like a maid running the country who only knows what the top says and the bottom listens, regardless of right or wrong, they support and flatter; If people feel miserable and complain, they keep it quiet and do not report it; Policies that have good things and benefits for the people are also avoided and not implemented; only cares about urging tax payment, calling it compliance with the law; Use the strict scrutiny of people to call it merit

clarity; That was the case that Mencius once refuted with all his words to those who always argued that "my king cannot do that". So how can it be called loyalty?

The object of "loyalty" is not necessarily just for the country's leader. Like the relationship between a subordinate and a superior, a maid and an employer, and all relationships between people, loyalty must be maintained. Below are two examples to highlight the meaning of loyalty.

Citing the story

Devotion to the Lord1

NOTE 1

Excerpted from the book A Ky Truyen (阿寄傳) by Dien Thuc Hoa. (Author's note)

During the Ming Dynasty, Chun'an County, Zhejiang Province, there was a Tu family, with brothers in the family dividing property together. The eldest brother got a horse, the next brother got a buffalo. The youngest brother passed away, leaving behind a widow, only the two brothers shared it with a servant named A Ky.

A Ky was over 50 years old at that time. The widow immediately cried and said: "Horses can be used for riding, buffaloes can be used to plow fields, the part I received from this servant is only for food."

A Ky immediately asked again: "Does the owner say that to say that I am not as good as a buffalo or a horse?"

From then on, he immediately replaced the landlady to think about how to make a living. The widow brought all her jewelry and sold it, getting a total of 12 taels of silver. A Ky took that amount of silver to the mountains to buy sumac tree sap to resell. In just one year, his capital increased 3 times. He traded again for another 20 years, accumulating a fortune for his widow worth tens of thousands of taels of silver. A Ky, on behalf of the landlady, married her three daughters, and invited a good teacher to teach her two sons. Later, they all married into famous families, the bride price amounted to thousands of taels of silver, and according to custom, they asked to be admitted to Thai school.

A Ky, every time he meets someone in the Tu family, even though he is young, he respectfully clasps his hands and bows. Throughout his life, he always maintained a dignified demeanor and never glanced at his mistress. For his master's daughters, even though they were young, he still maintained politeness and never stood on the same level. When he fell seriously ill and realized he could not survive, he brought all the management books and handed them over to the landlady, saying: "The two small owners can now take over the management of the family business. This old man has used all his oxen and horses to repay the master's gratitude. Now it is considered finished."

A Ky passed away, looking back at the place where he lived, there was absolutely no money or property belonging to the owner's house. His wife and one son only had enough clothes to cover their bodies.

Discussion

Keeping a heart like A Ky, fulfilling his duty like A Ky, planning a business for his master

living like A Ky, even if he is a great sage, he cannot do more than that. That such a person turns out to be just a commoner in a deserted village is truly amazing!

tieu_de: To parents, grandparents must be filial
noi_dung:
FOR PARENTS AND GRANDPARENTS, YOU MUST BE filial

Preach widely

Just that one word "filial piety", it's hard to say the full meaning! There is a saying in the Book of Poetry: “I want to repay all the kindness of my parents, but that kindness is so immense as big as the sky without end.” Truly, if children repay their parents, no matter how, can they reach beyond the sky? There are many books from ancient times that advise and encourage filial piety, but now only examples are rarely seen and rarely heard of.

If people don't know there is an afterlife and don't believe in cause and effect, it's just like a blind person who can't see or a deaf person who can't hear sound. Such a person is truly a miserable commoner who cannot appeal to anyone. Why is that? I don't know if there is an afterlife, and of course I don't know if my parents will have an afterlife, so even if I love and repay my parents with all my heart, it's only for a short, temporary period of time. I don't believe in cause and effect, of course I don't know that my parents will have cause and effect in the future, so even if I want to end suffering for my parents, I can only do a few small, limited things.

Once I saw a mother hen protecting her chicks and often took that as a reminder and a warning to myself. When the mother hen spreads her wings to protect her chicks, the love between mother and child is truly very deep. But after a while, people were killed one after another, causing mother and child to never have the chance to see each other again.

We as humans are actually not much different. Father and son, husband and wife, when they are together, it is truly difficult to separate and stay away from each other. But once the time comes for life and death to separate and the body to suffer from illness and pain, even the closest person cannot endure it for you; No matter how much evil karma you have created, no one can bear it for you. Even when it is time to let go of this body and enter the intermediate realm, facing thousands of sufferings, in this earthly world, our family members can be

re celebrating together. The blankets are still there, no matter how much I want to take care of them every morning and evening, I can't anymore; I don't know who to offer delicious dishes and strange things to anyone. Even if I learn from Vuong Tuong's "lying on the ice and catching fish" 1, what's the use? The ancients said: "A filial son cannot bear the death of his parents." So my parents actually never died. Is it just a lie to say something like that?

NOTE 1

Once upon a time there was a filial son named Vuong Tuong. His mother liked to eat fresh fish, but that year it was so cold that the water froze and it was impossible to catch fish. Vuong Tuong wanted a fish to offer to his mother, so he went to the river, took off his shirt and lay on the ice, wanting to use the heat of his body to melt the ice so he could catch fish. His filial piety touched the sky, causing the ice to naturally melt, and a pair of fish jumped up from the river for him to catch and give to his mother.

Buddha taught that: "The worldly people cannot fully repay the gratitude of their parents for their birth and upbringing. For example, if someone puts their father on their left shoulder, their mother on their right shoulder, and then walks like that for a hundred years, offering all their needs to their parents, they still cannot repay all of their gratitude."2 Thus, if we only follow worldly ways, no matter how hard we try, we will not be able to repay them. I can repay all my parents' gratitude! Considering this, we can be sure that in Buddhism there must be a perfect way to help people repay their parents' kindness.

NOTE 2

Because this is a Buddhist quote, we carefully found the content of this excerpt in the Tripitaka Sutra (雜寶藏經), in volume 2, starting from line 22, page 455, sheet c (Dai Chanh's new revision of the Tripitaka, volume 4, sutra number 203). Based on the scriptures, we translated this passage slightly differently from the original An Si Complete Book. This is the content of the sutra: 假 使左肩擔父右肩擔母, 行至百年復種種供養, 猶不能報父母之恩。(Left messenger Kien Dam father, right Kien Dam mother, practice half year, return seed palace due to his inability to repay his parents' kindness.)

Buddhist scriptures teach that: "The gratitude of the Buddhas is greater than the gratitude of our parents." But what is the meaning of being grateful to parents as extremely profound? Now, what does it mean to say that gratitude to the Buddhas is even more so?

In general, although gratitude to parents is deep, it is only limited to one life. Meanwhile, the Buddha's grace extends to all future lives. The gratitude to our parents is only to nourish this body, but the gratitude to the Buddhas is to save our intellectual and spiritual lives. Again, like the teachings of our parents, they only guide us on the path to fame and fortune. If we are confused and misuse them, we will create more karma. As for the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, they have absolutely no hope whatsoever. Therefore, in this world, the most serious ingratitude is none other than those who do not believe in Buddha and slander Buddha's Dharma. Lu Mong Chanh made a vow for such people not to be born as his descendants, and indeed had an extremely wise and far-reaching awareness.

Ly Tu and Thoi Hao were the two heaviest criminals in destroying Confucianism and destroying Buddha, so in their lives they suffered the extremely strange and tragic retribution of their own destruction. Tong

Huy Tong, although he worked to transform Buddhist temples into Taoist temples, did not destroy the Dharma, so even though he himself suffered humiliation, the country's fortunes were still continued. These are all very clear and verifiable stories from previous lives. May everyone in the world be able to understand the meaning of the widespread practice of following the Three Religions, whether those who follow Confucianism, those who follow Taoism or those who believe in Buddhism, all practice according to the teachings of their respective religions, working together in education, bringing peace to society, and no longer fighting and blaspheming each other. To be like that is truly extremely fortunate for all sentient beings.

Appendix 2 questions and answers about monks

Question: Monks do not spend any time plowing fields and weaving cloth, but just sit and enjoy offerings. It is a real waste of food and cloth in society. What benefits does this bring?

Answer: In society there are many types of people who do not plow the fields but still have food to eat, not just monks? For example, if they do not become monks, do they not consume food and cloth? If they consume food and cloth, do they have to plow the fields and weave the cloth themselves? What's more, if they become secular people, they are not alone, they must also have wives, children, relatives, servants to help... so the expense is many times more, how can

compare to the life of a monk who only has one robe and a bowl, here and there to educate people?

The people of the world use fox fur to make noble crowns; Brocade and embellishments make luxurious clothes; Going up to the high mountains and down to the deep sea to find all sorts of delicious and exotic dishes, the people who enjoy these things, on closer inspection, are those who don't plow but have food to eat. So let's ask, who are these people? Are you a monk? Are you a secular person?

In the secular world, concubines are loved when their body jewelry does not spare precious pearls; The royal singers and actors also wore jade belts and yellow hats; or like all-night casinos that waste money; or those who form gangs to party, drink and eat a lot... There are so many people who don't work but eat like that that you can't even use a cart to transport them or measure them all. Why don't you target them and eliminate them instead of just blaming the monks?

Is it possible that the worldly, evil, and lowly people enjoy brocade clothes and precious food, while the wise man who sees his true nature and clears his heart is not worthy of receiving coarse linen clothes and pickled rice?

I often hear people attacking people who disagree with me, and I can't help but feel a little dissatisfied.

Question: In ancient times, society had 4 components: scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants. Today's society has two more components: monks and Taoists, making a total of 6 components. One farmer uses six houses to eat, one produces goods to six houses, so how can one avoid poverty and theft everywhere?

Answer: If the number of people consuming food decreases, rice will not be able to be sold, and farmers will of course be harmed. If the number of people using the items decreases and the items produced cannot be sold, workers will also be harmed. Therefore, the farmer's source of profit lies in the fact that there are many people consuming rice, the worker's source of benefit is that there are many people consuming items.

Let's ask, can those who eat farmers' rice and use workers' tools to make it, blatantly take it for free? Or do I have to spend money to buy it? If only I didn't buy it but could use it, of course the more it is, the more harmful it will be. And if all users spend money to buy them and still think they are harmful to society, then would it be true that like big traders who sell goods worth thousands of pieces of silver every day, would their parents, wives and children see this and have to cry in pain? People who wonder like that are really old-fashioned, don't understand anything about life, and aren't worth talking about.

noi_dung:
HELP PEOPLE IN EMERGENCY
LIKE A STRUGGLED FISH; SAVE PEOPLE IN DANGER LIKE A BIRD KILLED IN A NET

Broad explanation

The concepts “danger” and “emergency” have a very broad meaning, compared to the previous text where it said “saving people in danger” is also synonymous. However, before, the Emperor narrated what he did himself, but here he teaches and advises people what to do. The word "like" used in this sentence has two meanings. One is used to compare two similar things, the other is used to compare the urgent thoughts in two similar cases.

Citing stories

ESCAPE, SAVE PEOPLE1

During the Eastern Jin Dynasty, around the reign of Thai Nguyen,2 in the capital city of Truong An, there was a man named Truong Sung who always believed in serving Buddhism. Since the reign of Emperor Xuan Zhao of the Former Dynasty

NOTE 2

The Thai Nguyen era lasted from 376 to 396.

Qin, Fu Kien, was defeated by the Eastern Jin and Chang'an, there were more than a thousand good households who wanted to flee to the south to surrender to the Eastern Jin, but were captured by the soldiers guarding the border. the desire to kill all the men, and capture and sell the women. At that time, Truong Sung was also arrested, his hands and feet were shackled, half of his body was buried alive in the ground. The next day, he planned to have soldiers on horseback use bows and arrows to shoot him to death, seeing it as fun.

Truong Sung thought he certainly could not escape death, so he could only recite with all his heart the name Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Around midnight, the shackles suddenly opened on their own, the body suddenly flew out of the ground, and immediately took advantage of the darkness to escape. Comment

If you yourself have not yet been able to escape, but you already have the mind of wanting to save others, that is the mind of a Bodhisattva. Truong Sung's wish was inherently compatible with Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara's wish, so his prayer must of course be fulfilled.

NOTE 1

During the Northern Zhou Dynasty, Dai Truyen Pagoda in the capital had a monk named Tang That, whose family name was Trinh, from Ham Duong, who was a true practitioner of morality. One day, at noon, he suddenly went upstairs and rang the bell very urgently, gathered the monks, and told them all to prepare incense. Everyone brought incense and asked the reason. He immediately taught: "At this moment, in Giang Nam at the temple... there is a lecture hall about to collapse, possibly crushing thousands of people to death. If everyone here unanimously recites the name of Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, that disaster can be saved." The monks obeyed, chanting the Buddha's name together, the sound echoed throughout the whole area.

A few days later, news came from Giang Nam. Sure enough, at noon the previous day, there was a lecture hall in Duong Chau holding a sermon, with thousands of people sitting inside. Suddenly I saw a strange cloud of incense smoke coming from the northwest,

along with clear, humming music. Incense clouds flew in from the north door of the lecture hall, then flew straight out the south door. The people in the lecture hall were horrified. They all rushed to follow the cloud of incense out of the lecture hall. As soon as everyone left, the lecture hall collapsed. Thanks to that, no one was hurt.

The King of the Luong Dynasty heard about this and came down three times to request an audience with him, but he did not come. In the 3rd year of Bao Dinh's reign, 1 on October 18, he passed away, and everyone in the court and family mourned.

NOTE 1

That is the year 563.

Comment

A sincere thought can create incense smoke, music, and in the blink of an eye reach a place thousands of miles away, from which one can understand the meaning "all is created by the mind". So how can it be said that cultivating blessings and praying for the salvation of souls cannot in the blink of an eye penetrate the dark underworld; that a person reciting the Buddha's name to seek rebirth cannot in a single moment go straight to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss?

quan in Lin'an, Zhejiang, including a medicine factory. One day, the medicine warehouse caught fire, and the fire spread to nearby people's houses. Commentary

Even if they themselves are guilty, worldly people still want to blame others, not to mention other people's sins that they firmly take on themselves, to the point of losing their official positions? The Prime Minister's generosity is truly immeasurable!

Helping the Redeemer GIVE CHILDREN1

NOTE 1

During the Ming Dynasty, Quang Binh district, Hebei province, there was a man named Truong Tu, whose family was poor and had no children. Truong Tu placed an earthen jar in his house and put all his savings into it. After 10 years, the jar was just full.

There was a neighbor of his who gave birth to 3 young children, broke the law, and was forced to sell his wife to get money to atone for his crime.2 Truong Tu knew about it, fearing that if the mother was sold, the 3 small children would have no one to take care of him, he immediately brought all his savings to atone for the other person's crime. Because that amount of money was still lacking, his wife immediately sold her brooch to make up for it.

Loving other people will eventually give birth to your own son. So we can know that if

harms other people's children, what will be the consequences?

tieu_de: Pity orphans and help widows
noi_dung:
PITY FOR ORPHANS,
HELP WIDOWS

Preach widely

Orphans, that is, children who no longer have a father. mother; Widows are women who have unfortunately lost their husbands. These two people are both single and weak, and are often easily overlooked and despised by people. If you don't pity and help those people, you truly have no compassion, can you be worthy of being human? Even if you can't help, you should always feel compassion and want to help. If you can help, you should wholeheartedly and truly help.

Be merciful and help, not necessarily providing money. It could be pointing out things you don't know, teaching things you haven't done yet, reminding people of things you shouldn't do, or even helping people overcome difficulties, clearing up confusing things, or clarifying injustices for others. Such things are also merciful and helpful.

tieu_de: Respect the elderly, love the poor

RESPECT THE OLD, PROVE THE POOR

Explain widely

Old age and weakness are inevitable, no one can avoid it, but it is the most pitiful reality. When people get old, their hair turns gray, their teeth fall out, and their bodies become thin and weak, with skin covering bones. The veins are clearly visible on the skin, the back is bent like a bow, everything that has happened cannot be remembered. On top of that, my eyesight was blurred and my ears were deaf. Every time I stood up or sat down, I had to rely on others for help. Therefore, when you see old people, you should respect them, not hate them. If you see old and weak people and feel disgusted and disrespectful, you should know that in the blink of an eye, you yourself will become old and weak. If you see old people and feel disgusted and disrespectful, you will not be able to live to old age!

Pity the poor! Everyone wants to eat well and dress beautifully, but they must

often suffers from hunger, starvation, and cold. Everyone wants to be satisfied, but they often have to endure misery. Although the cause of poverty is largely due to that person's own karma from previous lives, if we have the ability to help but do not help, isn't that teaching future children and grandchildren not to love each other? Providing for the hungry and needy is compassion for their immediate plight. Advise people to practice almsgiving according to their ability, which is compassion and mercy for people's next life.

During the Buddha's time, there was a merchant named Phat-gi-sa. One day, when he entered La Duyet city, as soon as he entered the city gate, he was gored to death by a female buffalo. The old woman knew what had happened and immediately chased after her. The three people loudly scolded her, saying: 'We have already paid in advance, why are we still asking for it?' When they meet again, they will kill all three of them to release their anger. The old woman from that time is now the female buffalo. The three traders from that time, now Phat Gia-sa and the other two, were killed on the same day by that buffalo."

That was really old and poor. Those three people, Phat-gata-sa... looked down on the old and weak, and did not know how to love the poor. When the right fate meets each other, if the old debt is not paid, how long will we wait?

In terms of relief methods to help during the lost famine season, there are rescue measures When it happens, there are also measures to help when it hasn't happened yet. For example, asking for tax reductions, preventing boats from transporting rice to other places, encouraging the opening of relief points to distribute food to the hungry, and prohibiting speculators from buying rice for profit... These are all measures when famine occurs. Clearing canals, strengthening dykes, encouraging farmers to develop agriculture, saving water resources, storing rice in case of rescue, recruiting people to clear waste land, strictly prohibiting river blocking to catch fish, slaughtering buffaloes... These are all rescue measures when famine has not yet occurred.

Applying measures when famine has not yet occurred will cost little but be effective, the people will be prosperous and the state will still collect full taxes. If we wait until a famine has occurred and people are starving to death in the streets, and then consider donating for relief, it will certainly cost a lot, and there will also be quite a few deaths.

tieu_de: Weighing and measuring must be fair, not selling short and collecting old

Every time you weigh and measure, you must demand and demand fairness, but you should know how to keep fairness in your heart, always consider fairness and take it as a standard. Introduction In the Dhammapada Sutra, the Buddha taught that: “Dharma

gift trumps all giving.” Practicing Dharma giving means sharing and spreading Buddha's teachings to everyone. Every Buddhist can, depending on their ability, practice Dharma giving in the following ways:

1. Try to learn, understand and practice the Buddha's teachings. The deeper you learn and understand, the more effective sharing and giving Dharma will be. Remember that reading books is more important than buying books.

2. You must cherish the scriptures and books printed with Buddha's teachings. When you have the means, buy them and bring them home so that you and your family can learn and follow them. You should not keep it as your own, but be willing to share it, spread it widely, and encourage many others to read and learn. You should not let the scriptures lie still and collect dust on the bookshelf, because if the scriptures are not read by people, they cannot bring benefits.

3. Depending on your ability, contribute material and effort to support those who do the work of compiling, translating, printing, and circulating scriptures, so that more and more precious scriptures can be printed and circulated.

Normally, spending a small amount of money cannot bring great benefits, but if used to help circulate If you practice the scriptures, the benefits will be unimaginably great. That's because it has helped many people understand and follow Buddha's teachings. I hope that Buddhists everywhere will pay attention to contribute their efforts to the above works.

ESSENTIALS OF PRACTICE OF Dharma Simulation

- Buy some scriptures to read, yourself will benefit a lot.

class="book-paragraph">- Sharing and spreading by lending and giving the scriptures to many people will increase the benefits many times over.

- Contributing effort and resources to support support the work of compiling, translating, explaining, printing, circulating scriptures the great merit cannot be measured, because countless people will benefit from the circulation of scriptures.
